Can you believe it? I went 15-0 with my straight-up picks last week. I guess it was an easy week, like some said. As for my picks against the spread, it wasn't quite as good, but it was better than it's been. I went 9-6 for the week, which I will take. The season marks are now 59-74-3 ATS and 87-48-1 straight up. Let's see if we can get perfect against the spread this week. Yeah, right. I will take three games above. 500 again as I make the climb to respectability. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Washington Commanders at New York Giants (-2.5) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime The Giants are back home after beating the Eagles and now face a Commanders team that probably has to win this to have any chance at the playoffs. The Giants' defense has been dominant up front as of late, and that will continue here as they contain Jayden Daniels . Giants keep winning. Pick: Giants 23, Commanders 14 New England Patriots at Detroit Lions (-2.5) Munich on Sunday, 9:30 a.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a big game for both teams, but especially so for the Patriots after they got blown out by the Packers at home last week. The Lions won at Miami and didn't play great, but they will get it going on offense here. New England is struggling on defense, so look for the Lions to win it with a strong offensive showing. Pick: Lions 30, Patriots 24 Kansas City Chiefs (-3.5) at Atlanta Falcons Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Chiefs snapped a two-game losing streak last week in beating the Jets , while the Falcons were blown out in Madrid by the Bengals . The defense had some major issues in that game. That will be the same here after the trade of safety Jessie Bates. Chiefs stack another victory. Pick: Chiefs 23, Falcons 17 Houston Texans at Cleveland Browns (+4.5) Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is a big game for both teams in terms of the playoff picture. The Texans looked dominant against the Chargers last week, but this is a second straight road game. It won't matter. Their defensive front will dominate whoever plays quarterback for the Browns . But the Cleveland defense will keep them in it. Pick: Texans 21, Browns 20 Minnesota Vikings at Green Bay Packers (-3.5) The Packers are coming off an impressive road victory over the Patriots and Jordan Love has been on fire. But the Minnesota defense is special and now they have Kirk Cousins to play quarterback. Even so, look for the Packers to win another one as their defense limits Cousins and the offense. Pick: Packers 27, Vikings 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-10.5) at Tennessee Titans The Titans are coming off a bye, while the Jaguars are coming off a victory last Thursday at Baltimore. They will be rested too. Jacksonville is riding high as one of the top teams in the league and made some moves at the trade deadline to get even better. Though this is a rivalry, with some unpredictable games, this won't be. Jaguars big. Pick: Jaguars 31, Titans 17 Miami Dolphins (+3.5) at Indianapolis Colts This is the dog game of the week between two struggling teams. But one is young and playing hard on the way up, while one is on the way down after trading away assets. The problem for Miami is that quarterback Malik Willis is out. That means Kyle McCord will start at quarterback. Miami will hang around against the depleted Colts team, but the Colts will win it late. Pick: Colts 23, Dolphins 22 Carolina Panthers at New Orleans Saints (-2.5) This is an enormous game in the division, even though both teams have just three victories. The winner will be in first place. The Saints beat the Browns last week, while the Panthers have lost three straight. The Saints make it four in a row as Tyler Shough has a big day. Pick: Saints 24, Panthers 21 Buffalo Bills (-8.5) at New York Jets The Bills are coming off a hard-fought road victory at Minnesota. The turnaround will be tough, but they are playing at a high level. The defense is improving. Look for Josh Allen to carve up the Jets' defense. Pick: Bills 34, Jets 21 Seattle Seahawks (-6.5) at Las Vegas Raiders Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) The Seahawks will start Drew Lock at quarterback again in this one. He was just OK last week against Arizona. But the Raiders have big-time defensive issues. For the Raiders, it's Fernando Mendoza time after they traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota. This is a tough defense for a first NFL start. Look for Lock to win it as the Seahawks' defense does the rest. Pick: Seahawks 24, Raiders 16 Los Angeles Rams at Arizona Cardinals (+9.5) The Rams lost at home to the Cardinals a few weeks ago and now must play without Puka Nacua . How will they move the ball? The Cardinals will start rookie Carson Beck at quarterback. Going against Myles Garrett and company can be a problem. Rams win it, but it's low-scoring. Pick: Rams 19, Cardinals 16 San Francisco 49ers at Dallas Cowboys (+4.5) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Cowboys can't afford another loss in their division race, so this is a huge game for them. The 49ers are riding high and that offense will challenge the Dallas defense. But I think the Dallas offense will be even better. Upset special. Dak Prescott has a bigger day than Brock Purdy . Pick: Cowboys 30, 49ers 28 Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals (-3.5) Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is for first place in the division. The Bengals are riding high behind their passing game and Joe Burrow . But the defense can't stop the run. The Steelers will run it here to keep Burrow off the field. It doesn't work. The Bengals will once again win it behind Burrow and the passing game. Pick: Bengals 27, Steelers 21 Los Angeles Chargers (+4.5) at Baltimore Ravens Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This game had promise before the season, but the Ravens are without Lamar Jackson and the Chargers are 0-8. Jacoby Brissett will start for the Ravens, which should help the offense some. The Chargers have struggled on offense, but I think their defense will keep them in this. It's close. Likely not, but they once again have a game against a bad team on Thursday Night Football when they face the Washington Commanders, and much like the majority of the season, I expect them to take care of business against an inferior opponent. These two teams played to a tie in Week 5 earlier this season, but with it being a road game for the Giants and the fact that they had Jameis Winston at quarterback, I think we can admit they're in a better spot in the rematch. J.J. McCarthy has been surprisingly solid to begin his tenure with the Giants, ranking fifth in the NFL in completion percentage over expected (+5.3%) amongst quarterbacks who have played 60+ snaps this season. It's also no coincidence that over the last three weeks, the Giants have led the league in net yards per play at +1.5. Now, oddsmakers have set a rather low total in Thursday’s matchup, even with J.J. McCarthy expected to start for the Giants against Washington star Jayden Daniels. The total is at 41.5, which suggests that we won’t see a ton of touchdowns in the opener for Week 10. Still, the anytime touchdown scorer market remains one of the most exciting ways to bet on the NFL, and there are three playmakers that I’m eyeing at plus money in this matchup. After all, the Commanders are just 19th in the league in EPA/Play on defense in the 2026 season and New York couldn’t slow down Daniels in the running game (two scores, over 100 rushing yards) earlier this season. Here’s a breakdown of my favorite anytime touchdown scorer picks for Thursday’s NFC East showdown. Best Anytime Touchdown Scorer Picks for Commanders vs. Giants Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Malik Nabers Anytime TD (+150) Malike Nabers has found the end zone just two times for the Giants in the 2026 season, but he’s been one a major part of the offense. The former first-round pick has 78 targets in eight games, reeling in 53 passes for 648 yards, and he was targeted 20 times in the tie against Washington earlier this season. Nabers found the end zone in that game, and this is a great matchup for him against a Washington team that is 18th in the league in passing yards allowed while also allowing the sixth-most passing scores (16). The Giants have thrown the ball a lot this season with their running game struggling, and Nabers has at least eight targets in four straight games. He should see enough volume to at least come near the end zone in Week 10. Stefon Diggs Anytime TD (+230) Washington wide receiver Stefon Diggs has five touchdown receptions in seven games this season, finding the end zone in four of his games. Diggs only has 30 catches in the 2026 season, yet he’s seen at least five targets in every game. On top of that, the veteran receiver didn’t play against New York earlier in the season and Washington struggled to get much going through the air. Still New York has allowed 14 passing scores this season, even though it did hold Daniels without a touchdown pass in Week 5. This price is pretty favorable for Diggs, who is by far the No. 1 receiver in this offense. The Commanders are running out of reliable pass catchers with Terry McLaurin and Dyami Brown both hurt. Isaiah Likely Anytime TD (+190) Giants tight end Isaiah Likely has been a touchdown machine in the 2026 season, reeling in 46 of his 69 targets for 448 yards and six scores. He’s coming off a score in Week 9 against Philly, and Likely has a couple of multi-score games in 2026. Plus, he’s been a beast when the Giants get near the end zone. In the red zone, Likely has nine targets in 2026, turning those into eight catches and five touchdowns. He hasn’t missed a beat with the New York quarterback changes, finding the end zone in Weeks 1, 5, 6 and 9. Yes, he scored against Washington in the overtime matchup in Week 5, catching 11 of his 13 targets for 94 yards and two scores. The Commanders have allowed eight touchdown passes to opposing tight ends in 2026 – the second-most in the NFL. At nearly 2/1, Likely is a great bet to lead this Giants offense once again in Week 10. Washington is coming off a 20-13 home loss to the Los Angeles Rams, while the Giants are coming off a 19-11 road win against the Philadelphia Eagles. The Commanders are averaging 21.5 points per game with a points-per-game differential of -3.75. The Giants have fared a little better, averaging 22.8 points per game with a 1.25-point-per-game differential. Just one of their wins (Week 4 vs. Arizona) has been by 10 points or more, which means the Giants have squeaked by so far. The good news for the Giants is their defense has been dominant. New York has allowed just 172 points to opponents this season, the seventh-lowest mark in the league, making a valid argument that the defense has carried the team for most of the season. What will this week bring? Let’s take a look. Another Divisional Win? Please. The Giants have not beaten Washington since 2023. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Giants erased the 13-year losing streak in Philadelphia on Sunday. This week, they have a chance to erase a five-game streak in which they haven’t defeated the Commanders, home or away. The Giants erased the 13-year losing streak in Philadelphia on Sunday. This week, they have a chance to erase a five-game streak in which they haven’t defeated the Commanders, home or away. The Giants and Commanders, of course, tied in their meeting earlier this year. Before that, the last time the Giants beat Washington was November 19, 2023. So they are long overdue. With a win, the Giants would improve to 3-0-1 in the division and remain a couple of steps ahead of the Dallas Cowboys, who seem hot on their heels in the NFC East race. So yes, a lot is at stake for the Giants, who are 1-6 in games played on Thursday night since 2020. The Giants are aiming for their second straight win on Thursday Night Football . New York Giants general manager Joe Schoen has been working the phones to try to get John Harbaugh additional reinforcements. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A short workweek is challenging enough, but throw in the trade deadline, and it gets even more complicated. A short workweek is challenging enough, but throw in the trade deadline, and it gets even more complicated. The Giants have been heavily linked to Colts running back Jonathan Taylor. Still, as of Sunday, Jay Glazer of Fox Sports reported that New York withdrew its offer after the Colts said they wanted much more for their lead back. That doesn’t mean that things can’t change, but it’s hard to see a deal happening, considering the Giants don’t have a 2027 fourth- or fifth-round pick to include in a trade, which appears to be a requisite to get a deal done. Given that the Colts also reportedly want a second-round pick, it’s hard to envision the Giants caving, especially after head coach John Harbaugh acknowledged the team isn’t one player away. And then there is the other side of the coin, which is defensive tackle. The Giants really haven’t been strongly linked to any defensive tackles, at least not in the way they’ve been linked to Taylor. Could a surprise move be coming? That said, it was a very positive-looking projection: not a single player among those appearing on the report would have been held out of practice. The Giants held a walkthrough practice on Monday, so their practice participation report was just a projection. That said, it was a very positive-looking projection: not a single player among those appearing on the report would have been held out of practice. That’s huge considering names like running back Cam Skattebo (hamstring), quarterback J.J. McCarthy (hip), receiver Malik Nabers (knee), outside linebacker Abdul Carter (knee/back), and tackles Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) are all on this week’s report. New York Giants quarterback JJ McCarthy exited the team's Week 9 win over the Philadelphia Eagles after taking a massive hit from linebacker Zack Baun. He eventually returned to the game after a trip to the locker room, but the team has since revealed if it could affect his playing status moving forward. According to NFL insider Adam Schefter of ESPN , McCarthy suffered a hip pointer and the team is confident that he will be ready for Thursday night’s game against the Washington Commanders. That is certainly good news, given how the injury initially looked. He was in visible pain on the sideline before heading to the locker room and being replaced by backup quarterback Jameis Winston. The Giants traded a 2027 fifth-round draft pick to the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for McCarthy following starter Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury in September. New York then switched to McCarthy as its starter ahead of its Week 7 matchup against the Houston Texans, and he has played quite well since, throwing for 622 yards, one touchdown and one interception.

home.headline: J.J. McCarthy injury update as Giants QB exits vs. Eagles
home.blurb: The Giants initially announced McCarthy was "questionable" to return to their Week 9 game against the Eagles before he returned to the game. The Giants have just two quarterbacks on their game-day roster, so Winston will be the last line of defense against the Eagles. Below is a look at New York's quarterback depth chart with Dart out for the season because of a knee injury. The New York Giants briefly lost quarterback J.J. McCarthy to an apparent injury in the third quarter of his second start with the team. McCarthy's injury occurred when he was scrambling to his left on a designed quarterback run. The 23-year-old quarterback was hit hard in the midsection by Philadelphia Eagles linebacker Zack Baun at the end of his run, and he remained on the ground in pain following the play. McCarthy was able to get to the sideline but appeared to be in a lot of pain. He was captured by the broadcast trying to throw passes, but he collapsed to the ground and grabbed at his right side after attempting a throw. He was then seen jogging to the locker room, with athletic training staff in tow for the team. Here's what to know about McCarthy's injury. McCarthy officially returned to the game for the Giants after missing the remainder of their go-ahead touchdown drive because of a hip injury. McCarthy completed 9 of 13 passes for 101 yards and added 11 yards on three carries before being injured. He will look to add to that total after returning to the field. Jameis Winston is the Giants' backup quarterback. He opened the year as the backup to Jaxson Dart and made four starts before ceding the starting role to McCarthy in Week 7. Winston posted a 2-1-1 record while completing 57% of his passes for 957 yards, seven touchdowns and five interceptions. He completed 6 of 8 passes for 71 yards while leading the Giants to a touchdown on his lone drive replacing McCarthy against the Eagles. Haener, a 2024 fourth-round pick by the New Orleans Saints, has made one career start. I went 14-1 straight up, and yes, I should probably just retire at this point, but I don't want to retire while I'm on top; I want to retire when I hit rock bottom, which might actually happen this week. Speaking of rock bottom, I went to McDonald's four times while I was in Spain, and let me just say, I only went there because Madrid had the nicest McDonald's I've ever seen. I mean, just look at this place. I'm now starting to understand why those Falcons players went to McDonald's. This is like the nicest McDonald's I've ever seen in my life. Wouldn't put it past Madrid to have a Michelin rated McDonald's #Bengals #Falcons #Spain https://t.co/w8WixT6iN2 pic.twitter.com/TMAeeXm9Fk There were also people tailgating inside of a Taco Bell. Taco Bell is in fact a mad house. NFL fans everywhere. Nothing like a pregame cheesy gordita crunch. #Bengals #Falcons #Spain #Madrid https://t.co/0uAafegmaM pic.twitter.com/cpjfyWy33X If you need just one reason to ever visit Spain, tailgating at Taco Bell has to be it. Unfortunately, there's no game in Spain this week, so there will be no tailgating at Taco Bell, but there is a game in Germany, and it will be the final NFL game of this year that kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET, which is definitely for the best, because I've reached my maximum limit for 9:30 a.m. ET games. The Patriots and Lions will be playing in the early game on Sunday. So who's going to win? Let's get to the Week 10 picks and find out. Alright, now let's get to the picks for real NFL Week 10 picks Commanders (2-5-1) at Giants (5-2-1) Thursday, 8:15 p.m. ET (Amazon Prime) Based on everything I've seen from the Commanders , I already know exactly how this game is going to play out: Washington is going to keep this thing close until the end only to lose (or tie) because no one in the organization has any idea what to do in any key late-game situation. For instance, let's go back to Week 5 when the Commanders pulled off one of the all-time worst late-game gaffes in a tie with the Giants . Washington had the game won. All Jayden Daniels had to do was literally anything except what he actually did. The Commanders can't get the play off in time and this game ends in a tie pic.twitter.com/WmPp6q5hU0 Look at the Giants players in that clip. They're celebrating. When the other team is CELEBRATING a tie, that means you lost. Surely Daniels and the Commanders learned their lesson, right? Wrong. In their Week 9 game against the Rams , they needed a 32-yard touchdown on the final play, but instead of throwing it in the end zone, Daniels threw the ball five yards past the line of scrimmage because the Commanders apparently thought they were going to be able to lateral the ball to each other all the way into the end zone. There's a reason that never works. With the game on the line Jayden Daniels can’t get the ball out of his hand. pic.twitter.com/2D8I1YWsiA Now, you could blame Daniels for this stuff, but ultimately, it falls on the coaching staff. In the Rams' game, Daniels said he was just running the play that was called . In the Giants' game, someone on the coaching staff should have made it clear to everyone on the field that the clock has to come to a stop on that play, whether it's a spike or a player running out of bounds. So what does this mean for this game? It means that the Commanders are actually playing decent football and if their coaching staff doesn't let them down, I think they have a good chance of winning. The Giants are beat up at quarterback, they're beat up at running back, and they're surviving by the skin of their teeth. Four of their five wins have come by one score. Good teams win close games -- are you taking notes, Commanders -- and I'm starting to feel like the Giants might be a sneaky good team. To me, this is arguably the most fascinating game of Week 10. If the Commanders lose, their season is all but over, but if they win, they'll be right back in the NFC East race. I feel like this is a pick I'm going to regret as soon as I make it, but I'm taking the desperate Commanders. PICK: Commanders 24-17 over Giants Patriots (5-4) vs. Lions (6-2) in Munich Sunday, 9:30 a.m. (NFL Network) With this game being played in Munich, I feel like this would be the perfect time to answer the one question that has been on all of our minds over the past few months: Who would win a beer-chugging contest between Mike Vrabel and Dan Campbell? With these two guys heading to the beer capital of the world, there's no reason not to find out. And to be honest, based on how the Patriots have been playing recently, Vrabel could probably use a few beers right about now. I'm not in charge of scheduling events for the NFL in Germany this week, which is probably for the best, but if I were, I would rent out the Hofbrauhaus and then give both Campbell and Vrabel one full stein of beer to chug. Instead of a coin toss on Sunday, this is how we would decide who's getting the ball first. I was at the Hofbrauhaus once and it took me an hour to finish my beer. The Germans were definitely laughing at me. What's the record for most beers drank in one sitting here? I think I'm going to try to break it. pic.twitter.com/UQ5kOtxyPL The Germans might be laughing at the Patriots, too, if they can't turn things around this week. Vrabel is known as one of the smartest defensive-minded coaches in the NFL, but he hasn't figured out how to stop any NFC North teams. The Patriots have faced two NFC North teams this year and not only have they gone 0-2, but they're surrendering an average of 37.5 points per game. Yikes. The NFC North is so good that I might not pick against any of their teams for the rest of the season unless they're playing another NFC North team. If you've looked at the NFL standings at any point over the past 24 hours, you may have noticed that the NFC North is arguably the best all-around division in the NFL this year and possibly ever. All four teams are at least three games over .500, which is the first time that's ever happened through the first nine weeks. Oh, and did I mention that the NFC North is 20-4 against all other divisions. They are destroying everyone. On the other hand, you have the Patriots, who are 3-1 against AFC East opponents, but 2-3 against everyone else. The Patriots have had one of the worst passing defenses in the NFL over the past several weeks, and now, they have to face off against a QB in Jared Goff who ranks in the top five in passing yards per game this year. The Lions might put up 50 points. The good news for the Patriots is that even if the Lions do put up a 50-burger, New England might still keep up. Detroit has given up the MOST passing yards per game this year (260.9), so Drake Maye could certainly get some turkey carving practice for Thanksgiving here by carving up the Lions' defense. That being said, I've decided not to trust Maye against good teams. The Patriots have faced six opponents this year with winning records, and in those games, Maye has thrown 11 interceptions to nine touchdowns. Based on how I think this game is going to go, Vrabel might need a Hofbrauhaus beer after it's over. PICK: Lions 34-27 over Patriots Texans (3-5) at Browns (5-4) Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (Fox) Deshaun Watson did not play in Week 9 for the Browns , but there's no chance he's going to miss this game. This is the ultimate revenge, though, I can't say for sure whether this is more about the Texans trying to get revenge on him or he's trying to get revenge on the Texans. Actually, now that I'm thinking about it, there might not be any revenge involved at all here. Since trading Watson to the Browns in March 2022, the Texans have made the playoffs three times, and they've won their division twice. On the other hand, Watson has been injured for the majority of his time in Cleveland; he's won just 14 games since 2022, and the Browns have paid him roughly $14.5 million per win. If Tom Brady had earned $14.5 million per win, he would have made over $3 billion in his career. Do you know how many Hofbrauhaus beers you could buy with that money? The worst part for the Browns is that they're still in QB purgatory, which is basically where they've been since returning to the NFL in 1999. Although Watson is playing well this year, especially late in games, I'm not sure that's a good thing. If he somehow leads Cleveland to the playoffs, the Browns might actually talk themselves into re-signing him, which doesn't seem like a great idea. away.headline: Patriots vs. Lions Wednesday injury report: AJ Brown returns, three ruled out
away.blurb: Wide receiver A.J. Brown was on hand for it. After missing back-to-back weeks due to a knee issue in addition to the high ankle sprain that sent him to injured reserve in September, the former All-Pro returned as a limited participant to begin Detroit Lions prep. But running back TreVeyon Henderson, offensive lineman Ben Brown and cornerback Carlton Davis III stayed among the sidelined in Foxborough and have officially been ruled out for the matchup in Munich. RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness — out) CB Carlton Davis III (knee — out) An illness that kept Henderson hospitalized for multiple days will now keep the running back out for a third straight game. The Patriots will be without another Brown on offense after the team’s starting left guard exited last Sunday’s 45-27 loss to the Green Bay Packers with a knee injury. And in the secondary, a knee injury will also keep Davis from taking the field in Munich after he’d worked back from a neck injury throughout October. That leaves four non-participants from Wednesday potentially in play for the NFL international series. FB Reggie Gilliam (knee — IR return) G Greg Van Roten (hamstring — IR return) S Kerby Joseph (knee — PUP return) But a pair of 21-day practice windows are now open for New England along with one 53-man roster spot. After Van Roten headed back to practice last week, Gilliam did so to start work on the Lions. The fullback spent the past five games on injured reserve. He marks the fifth IR return designation utilized by New England. NFL rules allot eight per club. The New England Patriots held practice inside Gillette Stadium on Wednesday before taking an evening flight overseas. Here’s the first injury report ahead of Sunday’s 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff at Allianz Arena. “There’s going to be guys that go to Germany that won’t play,” head coach Mike Vrabel told reporters prior to practice. No. 1 was among seven partial participants for the Patriots on Wednesday. The June trade acquisition hadn’t practiced since late last month and has missed six games altogether amid a season featuring nine receptions for 101 yards. RB Jacob Saylors (neck, hamstring) Under center, Maye continued to be a full participant for New England while carrying a listing due to his right shoulder. The reigning AFC Offensive Player of the Month completed 55 percent of his passes for 299 yards with three touchdowns and three interceptions last weekend. Prior to the blowout loss at home, the quarterback had turned the calendar to November by totaling three scores and only four incompletions in an AFC East comeback against the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium.

away.blurb: Chiefs Announce Major Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Before Falcons Game - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs Chiefs Announce Major Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Before Falcons Game The Chiefs deliver an update on quarterback Patrick Mahomes after the Jets game. Getty Max Dible · HEAVY Thu, November 12, 2026 at 12:53 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Kansas City Chiefs held their collective breath late in the first half last week against the New York Jets as superstar quarterback Patrick Mahomes left the field, clutching his throwing arm in obvious pain after a vicious hit to the elbow. In that moment, all of the team's hopes for its season, which started 5-0, might have been lost. Instead, the news has gotten progressively better with each update to the QB's health since. Mahomes returned to the game and didn't miss a single snap. He played well in the second half and Chiefs ran away with the win, breaking their two-game losing streak. The quarterback told media members after the game that he was not throwing the football comfortably or well early in the second half, though those issues improved as the contest wore on, adding that team doctors would conduct testing on Sunday after Mahomes finished with his media obligations. The MRI on his elbow came back absent any concerns of serious injury, which was the first bar for Mahomes to clear after he acknowledged that issues with that particular joint are often scary because of how unpredictable in nature they can be. Then, on Wednesday, November 11, Kansas City announced that its two-time MVP gunslinger was a full participant in practice ahead of the Chiefs' road matchup against the Falcons in Atlanta this weekend. "Chiefs listed QB Patrick Mahomes as a full participant in today's practice, putting him on track to play Sunday at Atlanta," Adam Schefter of ESPN reported on X . The author will update this post. The Texans are favored by 4.5 points, and the total is 39.5. The early forecast calls for temperatures around 45-46 degrees, winds near 10-12 mph with gusts around 16, and a 10-20% chance of rain. Nothing too serious, but it’ll feel like November football in Cleveland. The Browns have the better record, which makes this line interesting. Houston is favored because the Texans have been much better offensively. I think the oddsmakers have the right idea. With the NFL season heating up you should make sure you are fully prepared with our free NFL picks . Houston Finally Got the Offense Going Houston is 3-5 after beating the Chargers 44-22 on Sunday. That’s the kind of offensive performance the Texans have been looking for. They’ve had some frustrating losses, but scoring 44 points on the road should give them some confidence. The question is whether they can carry that into Cleveland against a defense that’s been better than the Chargers’ unit. The Texans are averaging 26.1 points and 356.5 yards per game. That’s good offensive production for a team with a losing record. Houston has been moving the football, but the defense and inconsistent execution have cost it games. The Texans need to avoid turnovers and make Cleveland play from behind. The Browns haven’t been scoring enough to consistently erase deficits, so an early Houston lead could be a big deal. C.J. Stroud remains the player Houston needs to lead this offense. When he’s getting protection, the Texans can move the football against almost anybody. The offensive line has to keep Cleveland’s pass rush from taking over the game. Houston also needs more balance from its running attack. If Stroud has to throw on every third down, the Browns have enough defensive talent to make things difficult. Cleveland Has Been Winning Despite the Offense Cleveland is 5-4 after losing 23-22 to New Orleans on Sunday. That’s a frustrating result because the Browns had opportunities to win. They’ve been competitive all season, but the offense hasn’t been producing enough points. Cleveland has been relying heavily on its defense, and that makes every offensive mistake feel expensive. The Browns are averaging only 17.9 points and 307.8 yards per game. That’s one of the lowest scoring averages in football. Cleveland has been doing a decent job controlling possession, but it hasn’t been finishing drives. Against Houston, that’s a problem. The Texans have enough offense to create a two-score lead, and Cleveland isn’t built to play from behind. Cleveland needs better quarterback play and more production from its running game. The Browns also need their defense to create pressure and force turnovers. That’s their best chance to win. If Cleveland can keep Houston around 20 points, the Browns have a shot. But asking the offense to score 27 or 30 is a different story. It hasn’t been doing that consistently. But the Browns are scoring fewer than 18 points a game. Houston is averaging more than 26. That’s a pretty big difference. The Texans just scored 44 against the Chargers, and I think they’ll carry some of that momentum into Sunday. Cleveland’s defense could make this uncomfortable, but I don’t trust the Browns’ offense to keep up. Give me Houston by a touchdown. Total Pick: Under 39.5 I’ll take the under 39.5. Houston just scored 44, so I know this looks a little strange. But Cleveland has been struggling to score, and the Browns will probably try to slow the game down. The weather shouldn’t be terrible, although the wind could make some throws more difficult. Houston can move the football, but Cleveland’s defense is capable of keeping the Texans from getting too comfortable. Something around 24-13 Houston makes sense. away.blurb: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans made it known that Montgomery's status has improved from last week ––when he was ruled out with a groin injury on Wednesday––but said he would continue to be evaluated throughout the week. It remains to be seen if he ends up playing once the weekend rolls around. Azeez Al-Shaair might be a name to keep an eye on, as he was a DNP with seemingly the same groin injury that's restricted his availability in practice as of late . However, given that he also had a personal designation, there's a better chance that he'll be good to go for either Thursday or Friday's session. Tight end Brevin Jordan also wound up as a DNP in practice with a finger/foot issue. If he's unable to go against the Browns, Houston has four other tight ends on the roster to turn to instead, including second-round rookie Marlin Klein, who was active on the gameday against the LA Chargers for the first time since Week 4. The Texans' final status for everyone on the roster will become clearer after Friday's practice. David Montgomery is the least surprising of the four, who has missed each of the Texans' team practices since leaving Week 5's game against the Tennessee Titans with a groin injury, and has gradually been working his way back to the lineup. The Texans also ended up seeing rookie offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge pop up as a rare entry on the injury report, as Coach Ryan’s noted that he had suffered a stinger during practice and would be listed as day-to-day. The stinger doesn't initially seem like something that would inhibit Rutledge's status for Sunday, but he'll have two more practices to go in order to see whether or not he'll be able to suit up. If Rutledge is indeed sidelined for whatever reason this weekend, veteran Wyatt Teller could be the primary name to look towards as Houston's next man up at left guard. But Blankenship is also dealing with a hand issue that might be making his return to play more complicated. Houston Texans Injury Report (as of 11/11) LB Azeez Al-Shaair (groin/personal) OG Keylan Rutledge (neck/shoulder) S Reed Blankenship (concussion/hand) DT Tommy Togiai (elbow/shoulder) The most notable takeaways from the Texans' first injury report of the week surround the four names who were listed as DNPs; three of them being starters. David Montgomery is the least surprising of the four, who has missed each of the Texans' team practices since leaving Week 5's game against the Tennessee Titans with a groin injury, and has gradually been working his way back to the lineup. The Texans also ended up seeing rookie offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge pop up as a rare entry on the injury report, as Coach Ryan’s noted that he had suffered a stinger during practice and would be listed as day-to-day. The stinger doesn't initially seem like something that would inhibit Rutledge's status for Sunday, but he'll have two more practices to go in order to see whether or not he'll be able to suit up. If Rutledge is indeed sidelined for whatever reason this weekend, veteran Wyatt Teller could be the primary name to look towards as Houston's next man up at left guard. He's started two games already this season in place of Ed Ingram

home.headline: Browns make big Shedeur Sanders announcement for Week 9 amid Deshaun Watson's injury
home.blurb: The Browns will start Sanders, even though Watson has yet to be ruled out for Week 9. He hasn't practiced much this week, and even if he does somehow clear concussion protocol, the Browns will roll with Sanders as the starter for one week. Cleveland could give Sanders the Week 9 and Week 10 start before the team's Week 11 bye, where they could figure out who should be the starting QB for the remainder of the year. But thanks to Deshaun Watson landing in concussion protocol, there is some uncertainty at the quarterback position for this upcoming game against the New Orleans Saints . Todd Monken cleared the air on the QB situation on Friday, as Mary Kat Cabot of Cleveland.com reports that Monken announced Shedeur Sanders will be the team's starting quarterback for Week 9. Shedeur Sanders announced as Week 9 starter for Browns "Browns Shedeur Sanders will start at quarterback vs. the Saints, Todd Monken announced," Cabot reports. This is some major news for the Browns, though it isn't a huge surprise, as a player clearing concussion protocol in the same week they were put on it doesn't happen very often. Sanders will now get a prime opportunity to prove himself worthy of being the starting quarterback this season. Considering Watson hasn't exactly been playing at a super high level, Sanders could make a real case to keep the starting job in Week 9. He will go up against a very leaky Saints defense that has allowed plenty of teams to put up very big offensive days. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images Christopher Gates · SB Nation Tue, November 10, 2026 at 2:13 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads After falling out of first place in the NFC North for the first time this season, the Minnesota Vikings will look to avoid moving into the division's basement when they head to Lambeau Field in Week 10 to conclude their home-and-home series with the Green Bay Packers for this season. The people who set the betting lines, apparently, don't like their chances. Our friends at the FanDuel Sportsbook have opened the lines for Sunday's game, and the Vikings currently sit as a 4.5-point underdog to the Packers. The over/under for the game currently rests at 42.5 points. The Vikings, as we all saw on Monday Night Football, appear to have completely abandoned the concept of offense, as they generated none of it in a 23-6 loss to the Buffalo Bills for their second loss in a row. Carson Wentz stepped in at quarterback for the injured Kyler Murray and turned in what may have been the worst start a Vikings quarterback has put together in recent memory, completing just 8-of-25 passes and turning the ball over three times, including two interceptions. . .a number that could have been significantly higher. The Packers, on the other hand, have won five of their last six after getting off to a 1-2 start. This past week, they absolutely thumped the New England Patriots to the tune of 45-27 behind three more touchdown passes from Jordan Love and a defense that forced Drake Maye into three interceptions. The Packers currently sit in last place in the North, but with a 6-3 record would lead either the NFC South or the NFC East. . .that's just how good the NFC North has been this season. These two teams met in the regular season opener at U.S. Bank Stadium. Wentz came into the game midway through the first quarter after Murray suffered a concussion, and the Packers had a 22-10 lead with just over five minutes remaining in the third quarter. From there, however, the Minnesota defense took over, leading an onslaught against Love and the Green Bay offense that saw the Vikings score 29 unanswered points to finish the game, including forcing a turnover on downs and generating an interception and a fumble to set up scoring opportunities. Minnesota took home the 39-22 win to get their season off to a 1-0 start. With the NFL trade deadline looming at 3:00 PM Central today. . .or approximately seven hours from when this story goes up. . .we will see if anything the Vikings do (or don't do) will shift this number at all. As it stands now, however, the Vikings are currently an underdog to their division rivals as the second half of the season officially gets underway.

away.blurb: For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . Minnesota Vikings general manager Nolan Teasley hinted Kirk Cousins could potentially jump right into the starting lineup beginning with Sunday's matchup at the Green Bay Packers. Teasley told reporters Wednesday it would ultimately be up to head coach Kevin O'Connell to decide which quarterback will start when Kyler Murray is healthy. "I would leave that to Kevin, he's going to put us in the best position to succeed," Teasley said. "But we also didn't acquire Kirk to not play." O'Connell discussed the situation as well: Murray was sidelined with a Grade 2 hamstring strain from Monday's loss to the Buffalo Bills, during which Carson Wentz struggled as his replacement. The Vikings acquired Cousins from the Las Vegas Raiders the following day. This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

away.headline: ‘They Fumbled It,’ ‘Vikings With the Heist’ — NFL Fans Mock Raiders After Packers HC Matt LaFleur Questions Kirk Cousins Trade Return
away.blurb: While the move gives the Vikings a much-needed answer at quarterback, the price Las Vegas accepted has left many wondering if the Raiders could have gotten more. Even Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur seemed surprised by the return. Matt LaFleur Questions Raiders’ Kirk Cousins Trade Return Naturally, LaFleur wasn’t alone in questioning the Raiders’ return. One fan argued that Las Vegas should have received at least a second-round pick. Another fan mocked the return, writing , “The Raiders traded Kirk Cousins, who is statistically like the 7th-best QB in the NFL, for basically a pack of peanut M&Ms.” Some fans also pointed out how badly Minnesota needed a quarterback. “Pretty obvious statement [from LaFleur] considering how good he’s been and how badly they needed a QB,” one user remarked. This fan also agreed with LaFleur’s assessment, writing , “I’m with MLF. You have the most desperate team in the league, and you let them off with a 3rd pick when you’re one game out of playoff contention? Seems [Explicit] weird.” The Minnesota Vikings made one of the biggest moves at the NFL trade deadline, bringing Kirk Cousins back from the Las Vegas Raiders on Tuesday in exchange for a 2027 third-round pick. The 38-year-old returns to Minnesota, where he played from 2018 to 2023, and reunites with head coach Kevin O’Connell. Speaking to reporters on Wednesday, LaFleur said, “I was surprised [Las Vegas] didn’t get more for him, quite honestly. I was shocked when I saw what they traded him for. It was mind-blowing to me.” Cousins is coming off a productive stretch in Las Vegas, throwing for 2,340 yards, 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions in nine games. He also posted a PFN QB Impact Score of 80.5, ranking 11th among quarterbacks through Week 9. “Honestly, I also thought it would be at least a 2nd. Throw away the whole Raiders franchise. The whole season, they were saying Cousins is the guy and just traded him for a 3rd-rounder,” they wrote . A second fan added, “Raiders had all the leverage, yet they fumbled it, lmaooo.” Others were less sympathetic toward Las Vegas’ front office. “No reason Raiders shouldn’t have bent them over for a 2nd. GM John Spytek is a media darling, but his actual actions have been underwhelming,” one commented. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Another added , “Raiders are stupid. Only a 3rd-round pick from a desperate team, lmao.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Another summed up Minnesota’s deal in just a few words: “Vikings with the heist.” Desperation in Minnesota Forced the Move The Vikings turned to Cousins after Carson Wentz struggled against the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football, completing just eight of 25 passes for 81 yards with two interceptions and a lost fumble in a 23-6 loss. With Kyler Murray sidelined by injury and Max Brosmer forced into action to finish the game, Minnesota needed a reliable starter. The team also terminated Odell Beckham Jr.’s contract

away.headline: Vikings-Bills Final Injury Report
away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Kyler Murray is out as expected, as are both Demond Claiborne and Jauan Jennings. Claiborne suffered a knee injury in practice and from Kevin O’Connell’s comments on Saturday, could be out for a while. It wouldn’t be surprising therefore if he was placed on Injured Reserve. It doesn’t appear at the moment that Jennings’ calf injury is a longer-term concern, but we may learn more about that next week. Beyond that, safeties Theo Jackson and Jay Ward are questionable for Monday night. I’m guessing at least one of them will play, but KOC also talked about potentially having Jacob Thomas and/or Tavierre Thomas on the active roster for Monday night to fill in at safety and special teams. For the Bills, backup wide receiver Joshua Palmer is out. But they also have two starting offensive linemen listed as questionable- left tackle Dion Dawkins and left guard Alec Anderson. Dawkins has not practiced all week with a rib injury, so he would seem to be less likely than normal to start with that designation. Anderson was upgraded to limited on Saturday after missing Thursday and Friday practices with an ankle injury. My guess is that if either of them play on Monday night they will be less than 100%, so the left side of the Bills’ offensive line could be a bit more vulnerable than normal. Beyond that, Tyrell Shavers and Jordan Hancock are listed as questionable, but the Bills will need to activate them from the PUP list and IR for them to be eligible to play on Monday night. We’ll see if that happens. home.blurb: During the loss to the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football, Cashman took a nasty hit that forced him out of the game. He returned to the field and missed only nine defensive snaps, but he is on the injury report with a concussion. Before the game against the Bills, Pace seemed like he was being phased out of Minnesota's defense. In the team's first seven games, he averaged only 8.4 defensive snaps per game and was mostly seen on special teams, where he played 21.7 snaps per game. Blake Cashman Injury Concerns Put Pressure on an Underused Viking to Step Up vs. Packers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs The Vikings could turn to another linebacker for help if Blake Cashman isn't healthy enough to suit up against the Packers in Week 10. But who? | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect Adam Carlson · Minnesota Vikings On SI Thu, November 12, 2026 at 12:00 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Vikings linebacker Blake Cashman is having a great season. Through eight games, he leads the team in tackles (76) while registering 10 quarterback hits, defending seven passes, getting 4.5 sacks, and recovering a fumble. Cashman needs to take as much time as needed to recover before he returns to the lineup, but the concussion puts his status for Sunday's game against the Green Bay Packers in question. If he is unable to suit up for Week 10, Minnesota will need Ivan Pace Jr. to step up. If Blake Cashman can't play in Week 10, the Vikings will need to rely on Ivan Pace Jr. On Monday night, Pace played the most defensive snaps of the season so far. He was on the field for 22 defensive plays and 24 special teams snaps, finishing with four tackles, one tackle for a loss, and one hit on Bills quarterback Josh Allen. Pace is the next man up for Minnesota. While rookie Jake Golday could be part of the inside linebacker rotation in Green Bay, the bulk of the work would go to the fourth-year defender with 27 games of starting experience. Cashman's absence would leave big shoes for Pace to fill, but he will be up to the task. This season, Pace has a 63.1 overall Pro Football Focus grade , but he is excelling as a pass rusher, earning a 90.0 PFF grade in that category. He tied his season-high with two pressures against the Bills, making it interesting to see if he can keep building momentum. Games between the Vikings and the Packers always seem to get more attention from fans and the media. Losing an important defensive piece like Cashman hurts defensive coordinator Brian Flores's unit, but the depth and talent on the roster can overcome it. Hopefully, Cashman will clear concussion protocol by Sunday's game, but if he can't, the Vikings need to have Pace ready for action against a tough division rival. home.headline: Injury timeline emerges for Packers RB Josh Jacobs
home.blurb: Packers medical staff tried multiple methods to protect Jacobs’ hand in hopes of getting him back on the field, but he was ultimately unable to return. Jacobs will undergo surgery to repair the issue sometime later this week. According to a report from NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport, he could return to the field for the Packers as quickly as 2-3 weeks. The earliest opportunity for Jacobs’ return is a Week 12 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams. While Jacobs could be back in a couple weeks, there’s also a chance his absence extends for a longer period. If the Packers decide to place him on injured reserve this weekend, he’ll automatically be ruled out for the team’s next four games. If that’s the case, his earliest opportunity to return would be a Week 15 matchup against the Miami Dolphins. Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs fractured his ring finger during the first quarter of this past Sunday’s Week 9 win over the New England Patriots. Green Bay is set for a division-rival matchup against the Minnesota Vikings this coming weekend. After that, the team will enter its Week 11 bye. Jacobs missed the first six games of the Packers’ 2026 campaign on the Commissioner’s Exempt List. The veteran running back recorded three total touchdowns in his two full games back on the field in Weeks 7 and 8. Backup RB Kaleb Johnson stepped up following Jacobs’ exit against the Patriots, rushing for 68 yards and a touchdown on 14 carries. The Packers, led by quarterback Jordan Love, furthered their reputation as one of the best passing offenses in the league. The Packers will kick off against the Vikings at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday. home.headline: Breaking down Packers' final injury report of Week 9 vs. Patriots
home.blurb: RB Chris Brooks (ankle): He is designated for return from injured reserve, allowing him to get in three days of practice this week. If MarShawn Lloyd can't go, the Packers could activate Brooks and play him Sunday. But as of Friday, he's not on the 53-man roster. RB MarShawn Lloyd (knee): He popped up on the injury report on Thursday but was able to practice again Friday in a limited capacity. Brooks is a replacement option, but the Packers have Josh Jacobs, Pierre Strong Jr. and Kaleb Johnson on the 53. CB Keisean Nixon (groin): He returned to practice on Friday after missing Thursday's practice, and it's difficult to envision him missing Sunday's game considering he still hasn't missed a game in his Packers career. It's possible he'll be a game-time decision based on how his groin is feeling in pre-game warmups on Sunday. EDGE Micah Parsons (knee): He only just returned to practice on Wednesday, and his most optimistic return date is still Week 12 against the Rams. Because he opened his practice window, the Packers are required to officially rule him out. The Patriots ruled out wide receiver A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) and running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness) and listed tight end Hunter Henry, safety Kevin Byard III, cornerback Carlton Davis III, receiver Mack Hollins, offensive tackle Morgan Moses, safety Brenden Schooler and offensive lineman Greg Van Roten as questionable. Fans wouldn't be blamed for forgetting that we've got football this coming Sunday after days on end filled with rumors and breaking news at the end of every sentence. Not only do the Titans play in Week 10, but they're hosting AFC South-rivals. The Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the most active buyers at the trade deadline, are coming to Nashville to boast their new pickups. The last time Tennessee faced Jacksonville, the Titans lost 41-7 at the very end of the 2025 season. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. Will: Cam Ward stays hot in Carnell Tate's return Ward nearly led Tennessee to a victory over the (now) 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. With WR1 Carnell Tate trending toward a return, Ward should have all of his weapons in place to put up another promising game. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. With a newly-gutted defense, the Titans will be relying on Ward to try and secure the win. Won't: Jaguars' overhauled defense clicks immediately Directly opposing Ward is that new-look Jags defense. In addition to adding All-Pro S Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville also acquired defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The south-most AFC South team sold off a ton of draft potential to make this happen, but the 6-2 team got a whole lot better as they sprint toward a hopeful Super Bowl appearance. Two out of the next three weeks, the Titans stand in the way. The south-most AFC South team sold off a ton of draft potential to make this happen, but the 6-2 team got a whole lot better as they sprint toward a hopeful Super Bowl appearance. Two out of the next three weeks, the Titans stand in the way. FOX Sports already had Jacksonville listed as a top 10 defensive team in the NFL prior to these trades. If Tennessee falls short (as is likely expected), it will be because the Jaguars' defense put a stopper in Ward and the offense's growth. That could be one reason among many, but it seems to be the most relevant by far regarding this specific matchup. Prediction: Titans lose, 34-23 At the end of the day on Sunday, I expect Jacksonville will overwhelm Tennessee. I don't believe it will be in blowout fashion, and this is primarily because of the stable flashes of progress Ward showed in Week 8. But between their overhauled defense and Trevor Lawrence manning things under center on offense, the Titans are truly facing a championship contender this week. Perhaps the home field will help blunt the blow, as well as the team debuting their Music City jerseys. I love the jerseys. I like what we saw from Cam Ward in his most recent game. But this Jaguars team has the AFC South in a headlock, and the 1-7 Titans simply don't have enough on paper to climb out of a double-digit projected loss in this one. picks.headline: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars vs. Titans: Which New Addition Makes the First Big Play
picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars vs. Titans: Which New Addition Makes the First Big Play Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- After a frantic start to the week that saw the Jacksonville Jaguars make the biggest moves of this year's NFL Trade Deadline, it is worth remember that the Jaguars do, in fact, have an opponent on Sunday. The 6-2 Jaguars are set to travel to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, their first game since making blockbuster trades for Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, along with adding Davon Godchaux for a sixth-round pick. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10. He is playing some of the best football of his career right now, and I predict it leads to another shutout. Tennessee Titans (1-7). The Jaguars have won five of their last six and are coming off consecutive blowout victories. The Titans were off last weekend but take the field having dropped two straight since recording their only victory of the season at Indianapolis back in mid-October. As is the case in most NFL games, the spotlight shines the brightest on the quarterbacks as we approach gameday. Trevor Lawrence is flourishing having thrown for 1,932 yards, 18 touchdowns and only four interceptions. He is an MVP candidate. Tennessee’s Cam Ward continues to labor under center having thrown for 1,483 yards with only six touchdowns and yet five interceptions. His future with Tennessee looks uncertain. Jacksonville’s latest performance was a convincing 33-10 Thursday-night victory at Baltimore, its second straight win by at least 23 points. Lawrence completed 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards and delivered the game’s biggest offensive play, a 50-yard touchdown to Parker Washington late in the second quarter that sent Jacksonville into halftime ahead 17-3. The Jaguars limited Baltimore to 227 total yards, forced three turnovers and kept the Ravens out of the red zone entirely; Baltimore’s only touchdown came on a 65-yard Justice Hill run in the fourth quarter with Jacksonville already leading 33-3. As noted earlier, Tennessee had its bye last week. It came at an ideal time after an exhausting 43-36 overtime loss at Cincinnati, arguably its best offensive showing of the season despite another defeat. The Titans jumped ahead 13-0 and took a 36-29 advantage with just 3:46 remaining when Ward hit Wan’Dale Robinson for a 15-yard touchdown and converted the ensuing two-point try, but Cincinnati tied the game with 1:17 left and won in overtime on Joe Burrow’s nine-yard touchdown run. Ward produced his first career 300-yard passing game, completing 26 of 40 for 304 yards and two touchdowns, while Tony Pollard ran 21 times for 117 yards and two scores. Tennessee accumulated 440 yards and forced four turnovers, including three interceptions by safety Amani Hooker , yet its defense was shredded for 510 yards and allowed Burrow to throw for 462 yards and five touchdowns before his overtime rushing score. The rivalry adds another layer because Jacksonville has emphatically reversed what was once a Tennessee-dominated series. The Titans still lead 35-28 all time, including their famous 33-14 victory over Jacksonville in the 1999 AFC Championship Game, but the Jaguars have won four consecutive meetings and seven of the last 10. Jacksonville swept Tennessee in each of the past two seasons, including a 25-3 win in Nashville last November and a 41-7 rout in Jacksonville on Jan. 4, 2026, the largest Jaguars victory in the history of the rivalry. away.headline: First Injury Report of Week 10: Dolphins Offense Could Be Even More Short-Handed Against Indianapolis
away.blurb: The Dolphins released their first injury report of Week 10 on Wednesday and what stood out was center Aaron Brewer not practice because of a concussion. While it's too early to rule out Brewer for the game against the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium, the fact he didn't practice Wednesday doesn't bode well. Based on the Return to Play protocol for players dealing with concussions, it's probably a must that Brewer practice Thursday on a limited basis for him to have a chance to play against the Colts. Robinson had to sit out the Week 2 game against San Francisco, while Proctor missed the Week 8 game against the New England Patriots. It should be noted that ahead of that New England game, cornerback JuJu Brents also missed the Wednesday practice because of a concussion before he was limited Thursday and a full participant Friday. He ended up playing against the Patriots. The other issue to monitor on offense involves rookie wide receiver Chris Bell, who is back on the injury report with limited participation in practice because of a knee issue. Quarterback Kyle McCord is set to make his NFL debut for the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, but it might have to do without having the team's All-Pro center snapping him the ball. And rest assured the Dolphins will be very careful not to rush him into action. The Dolphins unfortunately are becoming accustomed to having to deal with concussions, as both edge defender Chop Robinson and guard Kadyn Proctor missed a game this season because of that issue. Brewer played every snap against the Lions during the 19-9 loss Sunday, so this llikely was another case of him reporting symptoms the following day. The other player on the 53-man roster who didn't practice Wednesday was rookie tight end Will Kacmarek, who is dealing with quad/knee issues. He left the game against Detroit after taking a big shot to the side of the leg after a short reception and was seen at practice Wednesday wearing a compression sleeve on his left leg. If he were unable to play against Indianapolis, it likely would mean more reps for fellow rookie Seydou Traore, who's gotten more involved on offense is recent weeks and also would mean an appearance by waiver wire pick-up Justin Joly. Bell, who is nearing the one-year anniversary of the torn ACL he sustained in his final season at Louisville, last was on the injury report before the Week 5 game against the Cincinnati Bengals. It's logical to think, though not certain, he's dealing with some soreness in his surgically repaired knee. That obviously isn't a great development after he wasn't on the injury report at all for the past three games. Bell played 36 offensive snaps against Detroit after playing 45 against the New England Patriots. He was targeted only once against the Lions, the result being an incomplete pass. home.headline: Dolphins add QB Malik Willis to IR due to lingering groin injury; Kyle McCord expected to start vs. Colts
home.blurb: Dolphins add QB Malik Willis to IR due to lingering groin injury; Kyle McCord expected to start vs. Colts - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs Teddy Ricketson Contributing writer Tue, November 10, 2026 at 9:27 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Miami Dolphins announced Tuesday that they are placing quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve . Willis has had a lingering groin injury that has been impacting his mobility. The quarterback had an MRI, and it showed that it is now a core muscle injury. Willis doesn't need surgery, but the amount of rest required to recover necessitated an IR stint. With Willis sidelined for at least the next month, backup quarterback Kyle McCord is expected to take over as the starter this weekend against the Indianapolis Colts, per ESPN's Adam Schefter . Willis is not expected to miss the remainder of the season. Willis joined the Dolphins this offseason, signing a 3-year, $67.5 million deal in free agency. He reunited with new Miami head coach Jeff Hafley, who was with Willis last year in Green Bay as the defensive coordinator. Willis has played in eight games this season and has thrown for 1,396 yards, 6 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. The 27-year-old is known for being able to use his legs and has picked up 232 yards and three additional scores on the ground. Willis is currently Miami's second-leading rusher behind Ollie Gordon (463 yards, 4 TDs). McCord was a sixth-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft by the Philadelphia Eagles. He spent the season on Philadelphia's practice squad, but joined the Packers in the offseason on a reserve/futures contract. The quarterback was then traded to the Dolphins in late August for a 2028 sixth-round pick to replace Quinn Ewers, whom Miami traded to the Jacksonville Jaguars. McCord has yet to play a snap in his pro career, but that is expected to change Sunday against the Colts, as he is in line to make his first career start. Brady Cook is currently Miami's only other quarterback, and he is on the practice squad.

away.headline: Travis Etienne Jr. returns on first Saints-Panthers injury report
away.blurb: Here we go. Just like wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and Kevin Banks Jr. did last week, New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne Jr. practiced on a limited basis on the first injury report of Week 10. He'll have a chance to play on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers depending on how his leg responds throughout the week. Etienne has been on injured reserve since Week 3's loss to the Las Vegas Raiders after injuring his hamstring. As for the rest of the Week 10 injury report? The Saints listed Banks (ankle), left guard David Edwards, cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (shin), tight end Noah Fant (back), and rookie defensive tackle Christen Miller (knee) as other limited participants, while swing tackle Asim Richards (thumb) practiced fully. Kamara was given a rest day while Donaldson and center Erik McCoy (biceps) did not participate. McCoy is expected to miss some time. We'll be looking for updates when the Saints share their next injury report on Thursday afternoon. The backfield has shaken up in his absence. New Orleans waived Kendre Miller and brought back Audric Estime while Alvin Kamara (back) and CJ Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) have dealt with other injuries. Etienne signed a lucrative contract in free agency and should be the top option at running back once healthy. away.headline: Carolina Panthers See Three Players Return to Practice
away.blurb: Carolina Panthers See Three Players Return to Practice - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Carolina Panthers See Three Players Return to Practice The Panthers welcomed three key players back to practice on Wednesday: Running back Jonathon Brooks, defensive back Mike Jackson, and wide receiver Xavier Lagette. All three have been on injured reserve, but now the practice window to return is here and the Panthers are hoping they can get back on the field sooner than later. On offense, the Panthers really need to get Brooks back at the running back position. Since he's been out, it's been mainly Chuba Hubbard taking the lead role. If Brooks can return soon, it will help take some of that pressure off of Hubbard and give the Panthers another fresh option in the backfield for their offense. Brooks has been out since September 23rd and underwent surgery to repair a core muscle injury. He was listed as a full participant on Wednesday. Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs (REUTERS) Zack Pearson · Roundtable Sports Thu, November 12, 2026 at 3:15 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads The Carolina Panthers had a quiet NFL Trade Deadline day, opting not to make any moves and instead standing pat. With a 3-5 record, the Panthers are tied atop the NFC South as every team in the division has three wins going into this weekend. As Carolina looks to repeat as division champions, a good start would be winning their Week 10 showdown in New Orleans against the Saints. Carolina at one point was 3-2 but a three-game losing streak that featured some tough injuries has set them back a bit. But there appears to be good news on the horizon. Carolina will now monitor each player in terms of when they can be officially activated and added to the roster. But the good news is that returns are looming for each of them and they are at key positions in which the Panthers really need help. Wide receiver Xavier Lagette suffered a knee injury and hasn't played since September 20th. With Carolina relying on the duo of Tetairoa McMillan and Jalen Coker, they could use some depth at the position as well. As for Jackson, his injury was significant. He's one of Carolina's top defensive backs and started in the first three games of the season before getting hurt. Carolina is also down Jaycee Horn in the secondary and in their loss to Green Bay they were down to some second and third string defensive backs. Carolina's defense could be the key to winning the division, so the sooner Jackson is back to play, the better. With the 21-day window now open, the Panthers will have these three weeks to activate them to the roster.

home.headline: Travis Etienne Jr. returns on first Saints-Panthers injury report
home.blurb: Here we go. Just like wide receiver Jordyn Tyson and Kevin Banks Jr. did last week, New Orleans Saints running back Travis Etienne Jr. practiced on a limited basis on the first injury report of Week 10. He'll have a chance to play on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers depending on how his leg responds throughout the week. Etienne has been on injured reserve since Week 3's loss to the Las Vegas Raiders after injuring his hamstring. As for the rest of the Week 10 injury report? The Saints listed Banks (ankle), left guard David Edwards, cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (shin), tight end Noah Fant (back), and rookie defensive tackle Christen Miller (knee) as other limited participants, while swing tackle Asim Richards (thumb) practiced fully. Kamara was given a rest day while Donaldson and center Erik McCoy (biceps) did not participate. McCoy is expected to miss some time. We'll be looking for updates when the Saints share their next injury report on Thursday afternoon. The backfield has shaken up in his absence. New Orleans waived Kendre Miller and brought back Audric Estime while Alvin Kamara (back) and CJ Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) have dealt with other injuries. Etienne signed a lucrative contract in free agency and should be the top option at running back once healthy. Dak Prescott is playing well, CeeDee Lamb has proven his status as one of the best wide receivers in the NFL, and Javonte Williams is proving his 2025 breakout was for real. However, there is one problem on this Cowboys' offense that needs addressing. That issue is the team's backup running back spot. After some early-season roster shuffling, Tyler Goodson emerged as the clear No. 2 RB in Dallas. But he's hurt and will miss time. That has led the Cowboys to make an interesting signing. While they could've turned to the trade deadline and tried to acquire someone like Tony Pollard, they opted instead to sign the recently released Kendre Miller. The 24-year-old running back has just 656 rushing yards and five touchdowns on 184 attempts in four seasons with the Saints. He was cut prior to Week 9 and has quickly found a home in Dallas. With Williams being the clear lead back, and Goodson hurt, Miller should be activated off the practice squad and be penciled in as the No. 2 back starting in Week 10. Dallas needs RB depth, and Miller, a fourth-year RB who's shown some promise at times with the Saints, is an intriguing pickup for the Cowboys offense. He might not be a needle-moving addition, like some teams around the NFL made at this year's trade deadline. But with Miller added to the depth chart, the Cowboys have an intriguing upside option to turn to when they give Williams a rest. Miller isn't on the 53-man roster, so the Cowboys have to activate him for Sunday's matchup against the San Francisco 49ers if they believe he's ready to go. Miller, once active, will serve as Williams' backup until Goodson returns from injury.
