home.headline: Travis Etienne Jr.'s Practice Return Creates Murky Fantasy Football Situation in the New Orleans Saints' Backfield
home.blurb: The Saints Backfield Shuffle: What Travis Etienne’s Impending Return Means for Fantasy Football Managers Now, with the Saints opening his 21-day practice window, the team will "see how the week plays out" before determining if he is ready to suit up for a crucial divisional clash. While Etienne's return is a welcome boost for a New Orleans offense looking to secure the NFC South crown, it introduces a major headache for fantasy managers holding shares of Alvin Kamara and breakout waiver wire darling Audric Estime. However, managers should temper expectations for his immediate return. Hamstring injuries are notoriously tricky for running backs, and Kellen Moore's cautious tone suggests they may ease him back into the rotation (if he even plays against the Carolina Panthers this week). Etienne's impending return is bad news for fantasy managers planning on relying on Alvin Kamara or Audric Estime down the stretch. During Etienne's lengthy five-game absence, the Saints' backfield morphed into a shifting puzzle. Alvin Kamara has continued to command a steady role, but his efficiency and volume have fluctuated. An active Etienne directly eats into his touches, explosive play opportunities, and red-zone looks that anchor Kamara’s weekly floor. While Kamara’s skill set keeps him relevant, his path to anything more than risky flex numbers narrows significantly once Etienne assumes his starting workload. Audric Estime is even more vulnerable. He capitalized on the depleted depth chart to carve out an expanded role and became a popular waiver-wire pickup this week, but a healthy Etienne completely caps Estime’s fantasy football utility. Without an outright injury ahead of him on the depth chart, Estime projects to slide back into a game-script-dependent rotational role, making him difficult to trust in most leagues. If you roster Travis Etienne, hold tight and make sure he is stashed safely in your active or IR spot as he nears a game-day designation. If you are relying on Alvin Kamara, prepare for a hit to his weekly ceiling as touches are redistributed. As for Audric Estime managers, it might be time to treat him strictly as a high-end handcuff. The Saints are still very much in the NFC South playoff hunt, and how this three-way backfield shakes out as part of their playoff push will dictate fantasy championships across the board. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton The Buffalo Bills (7-1) visit the New York Jets (2-7) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium, with the AFC East rivals heading in dramatically different directions. Buffalo sits three games clear of second-place New England atop the division while the Jets have lost four in a row and sit but a half-game out of the cellar in the AFC East. The Bills enter the week with the NFL’s highest-scoring offense at 32.0 points per game and lead the league with 386.4 yards per game, powered by Josh Allen and a rushing attack featuring James Cook III . The Jets, meanwhile, are averaging just 20.2 points per game which begs the question: Can Geno Smith and the Jets score enough to keep up with the Bills’ elite attack? Working in the Jets’ favor is that Buffalo has a short turnaround after grinding out a 23-6 road victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night. It was a far more physical game than the final score suggests. The Bills managed just three points on their first six possessions, and Allen threw an early interception, but his 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds remaining in the first half gave Buffalo a 10-6 advantage. From there the Bills wore down Minnesota, holding the ball for an extraordinary 42:32 and running 79 offensive plays. Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards, including a five-yard fourth-quarter touchdown, while Allen finished 21-of-31 for 234 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Buffalo’s defense was even better, limiting Minnesota to 178 total yards and nine first downs while forcing three turnovers. The Jets return home after a 35-12 loss at Kansas City. Despite an early 6-0 lead, New York’s offensive woes were impossible to ignore. Smith and co. repeatedly stalled and had to settle for four Jason Sanders field goals. The Chiefs led just 14-12 at halftime before completely controlling the second half. New York finished with only 229 yards, went 2-for-12 on third down and failed to score a touchdown, while Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards and was sacked five times. Breece Hall returned from a five-game absence caused by a quadriceps injury and produced 87 yards from scrimmage, while rookie Omar Cooper Jr. led the Jets with eight catches for 58 yards. Recent history adds another challenge for New York. Buffalo has won eight of the past 10 meetings, including a couple smacks last season, beating the Jets 30-10 at MetLife Stadium on Sept. 14, 2025 and 35-8 in Buffalo on Jan. 4, 2026. home.headline: Bills vs. Jets prediction: Odds, expert picks, QB matchup, injury update, trends, and stats
home.blurb: The Buffalo Bills (7-1) visit the New York Jets (2-7) on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium, with the AFC East rivals heading in dramatically different directions. Buffalo sits three games clear of second-place New England atop the division while the Jets have lost four in a row and sit but a half-game out of the cellar in the AFC East. Working in the Jets’ favor is that Buffalo has a short turnaround after grinding out a 23-6 road victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday night. It was a far more physical game than the final score suggests. The Bills managed just three points on their first six possessions, and Allen threw an early interception, but his 25-yard touchdown pass to Keleki Latu with 44 seconds remaining in the first half gave Buffalo a 10-6 advantage. From there the Bills wore down Minnesota, holding the ball for an extraordinary 42:32 and running 79 offensive plays. Cook carried 31 times for 107 yards, including a five-yard fourth-quarter touchdown, while Allen finished 21-of-31 for 234 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Buffalo’s defense was even better, limiting Minnesota to 178 total yards and nine first downs while forcing three turnovers. The Jets return home after a 35-12 loss at Kansas City. Despite an early 6-0 lead, New York’s offensive woes were impossible to ignore. Smith and co. repeatedly stalled and had to settle for four Jason Sanders field goals. The Chiefs led just 14-12 at halftime before completely controlling the second half. New York finished with only 229 yards, went 2-for-12 on third down and failed to score a touchdown, while Smith completed 18 of 32 passes for 165 yards and was sacked five times. Breece Hall returned from a five-game absence caused by a quadriceps injury and produced 87 yards from scrimmage, while rookie Omar Cooper Jr. led the Jets with eight catches for 58 yards. Hall has missed five games with a quad muscle injury, while Bailey was out for the Las Vegas Raiders game with a groin injury. Ossai has been in and out of the lineup, most recently with an ankle injury. Hall's return has been eagerly anticipated for several weeks, although big back Braelon Allen has filled in more than capably in his absence. Trade rumors are floating about Hall being dealt before the Nov. 10 NFL trade deadline, but the Jets are adamant that he's not going anywhere. His return also raises the question of how he will be deployed alongside Allen, although the latter was seen walking gingerly on the sidelines of the Raiders game in the second half. That may factor into how they will be used, although Allen is not on the official injury report. Bailey would be a big help on a depleted Jets defense. Defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat is on injured reserve, leaving Harrison Phillips and Darrell Jackson Jr. as the men in the middle, a slight drop off from Sweat's massive presence. Phillips has an ankle injury and did not practice on Thursday, not a great sign for his availability in the upcoming game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Backup linebacker Trevin Wallace is also on the injury report with a groin injury. He was listed as limited in the report. Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs Bruce Haring · Athlon Sports Thu, November 5, 2026 at 5:10 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Good news is in short supply around the 2-6 New York Jets right now. But there was a bit of green shoots for Gang Green in their Thursday injury report. A bigger concern for the Jets is the absence of wide receiver Garrett Wilson, who is in the NFL concussion protocol. Wilson was injured on the next-to-last play of the Raiders game, but played the final snap. He came in on Monday complaining of symptoms. He will now have to pass the rigid NFL protocols before returning to action. Receivers Adonai Mitchell, Omar Cooper Jr. and the tight end tandem of Taylor and Kenyon Sadiq will try to fill the breach, but Wilson is a superstar talent that can change a game when properly used. The Jets will need as many of their frontline talents as they can muster against the Chiefs. The NY team is 9.5 underdogs on the road at Arrowhead Stadium, and they will confront a Chiefs team still smarting from a loss to the Denver Broncos.

The Raiders have one of the worst defenses in the NFL, particularly when it comes to stopping the run. However, this matchup could be exactly what he needs to change the trajectory of his season. The Raiders have struggled mightily against opposing running backs, and Price should have opportunities to make an impact. The Raiders have struggled to contain opposing offenses. I think he gets back to dominating opposing secondaries. Mendoza does have some talented tight ends to work with, but Las Vegas' receiving corps is underwhelming. Seattle should be able to make things uncomfortable for the rookie, particularly if its pass rush can consistently generate pressure. It wouldn't be surprising if Mendoza throws a touchdown pass at some point. However, I expect the Raiders' offense to struggle for most of the afternoon. The prediction is that Mendoza finishes with fewer than 175 passing yards and completes less than 65% of his attempts. His first NFL start will be a difficult learning experience, and Seattle's defense will be the biggest reason why. (4-5) are looking to rebound from one of their sloppiest performances of the season AND are looking to do so with rookie Fernando Mendoza making his first start of his career. The matchup is a monster challenge for Mendoza: Seattle has leaned on a defense allowing just 18.0 points per game, tied for fourth-best in the league entering the week, while Las Vegas has surrendered 29.8 per game, ranking last. So you expect the Raiders would look to lean on Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr. to run the ball and take the pressure off their rookie signal-caller…but know that the Seahawks allow an average of 89.1 yards per game (151.2 for the Raiders). Quarterback is also a storyline for the Seahawks. Sam Darnold remains sidelined with a quad injury after also reportedly cracking a rib against Chicago, while Drew Lock came out of this past Sunday’s game dealing with an oblique issue after previously battling elbow tendinitis. Seattle comes in off a much-needed 17-3 victory over Arizona, a game it controlled despite playing without starting quarterback Darnold. Backup Lock completed 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown, while tight end AJ Barner supplied both Seattle touchdowns, catching one from Lock and running for another. Zach Charbonnet , recently returned from an ACL injury, gave the offense some balance with 77 yards on 16 carries, and the defense held Arizona to 216 total yards and no touchdowns. Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught seven passes for 51 yards and became the first NFL receiver to reach 1,000 yards this season. Las Vegas, meanwhile, is trying to clean up the turnovers after a 38-17 loss at San Francisco dropped it below .500. The Raiders were actually within 21-10 at halftime, but Kirk Cousins was intercepted on the first play of the third quarter and Jaden Dugger returned it 35 yards for a touchdown, beginning a disastrous second half. Cousins finished 22-of-32 for 216 yards, one touchdown and three interceptions as Las Vegas committed five turnovers, managed only 240 total yards and 24 rushing yards, and possessed the ball for just 21:42. Brock Bowers was possibly the only bright spot, catching seven passes for 111 yards and a touchdown. Sunday’s game is also a reunion of two franchises with considerably more history than their present-day conference alignment suggests. The Raiders and Seahawks were AFC West rivals from 1977 through 2001, and the Raiders lead the overall series 30-26, including postseason games. They have met only periodically since Seattle moved to the NFC, with the last meeting producing one of the wildest games of the 2022 season: the Raiders won 40-34 in overtime in Seattle, powered by Josh Jacobs’ 229 rushing yards and two touchdowns. Seahawks vs. Raiders Week 10 predictions: Jaxon Smith-Njigba First TD odds as Klint Kubiak faces his old offense
picks.blurb: Seahawks vs. Raiders Week 10 predictions: Jaxon Smith-Njigba First TD odds as Klint Kubiak faces his old offense - oregonlive.com Skip to Article Set weather Back To Main Menu Close Weather in - Change Location Current - Mostly Sunny Tonight Low - Mostly Sunny Tomorrow High - Mostly Sunny Full Weather Report Sports Betting Published: Nov. 11, 2026, 9:15 a.m. Sina Torki | Special Correspondent Klint Kubiak called the plays for Seattle’s Super Bowl offense last season. On Sunday he sees that offense from the other sideline. Kubiak’s Las Vegas Raiders (4-5) host the Seahawks (5-4) at Allegiant Stadium, and the betting market has spent the week moving toward his team. DraftKings opened Seattle as a 7-point favorite, according to ESPN . Bet365 now has the Seahawks at -3.5. Seattle comes in off a 17-3 home win over Arizona. Las Vegas lost 38-17 at San Francisco. The records and recent form favor the Seahawks, but the line movement says the market thinks this is much closer to a field-goal game than it first looked. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is again the shortest price to score first, though at a longer number than he was against the Cardinals. Teams: Seattle Seahawks at Las Vegas Raiders Date: Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026 Kickoff: 1:05 p.m. PT (4:05 p.m. ET) Location: Allegiant Stadium, Las Vegas TV: CBS ( Seahawks viewing guide ) Records: Seahawks 5-4, Raiders 4-5 More: NFL.com game center · NFL standings · NFL injury reports Seahawks vs. Raiders odds Odds are from Bet365 and are accurate at time of publication. Spread: Seahawks -3.5 (-105), Raiders +3.5 (-115) Moneyline: Seahawks -182, Raiders +152 Total: Over 43.5 (-105), Under 43.5 (-115) The moneyline implies roughly 64.5% for Seattle. The spread and total together point to a final around Seahawks 23.5, Raiders 20. Las Vegas is the more expensive side of the spread at -115, a sign the market still sees value in the hook even after three and a half points of movement. Jaxon Smith-Njigba to score the first touchdown (+425) Bet365 has Smith-Njigba at +425 to open the scoring , an implied probability of roughly 19.0%. His -130 anytime price implies roughly 56.5%. He was +350 to score first against Arizona last week, so the market has lengthened him in a game it expects to be closer and played on the road. He leads Seattle with 1,036 receiving yards and nine touchdowns, per NFL.com , and is the only player on this board priced shorter than even money to score at any point. The gap to the rest of the board is narrower than last week. Zach Charbonnet is +600 to score first (roughly 14.3%) and Brock Bowers is +625 (roughly 13.8%), both about five points behind. On the anytime market, Charbonnet and Bowers are both +115 (roughly 46.5%), 10 points back. Bowers is the case against. The Raiders score 26.4 points per game, eighth in the league, four more than Seattle’s 22.4. Kirk Cousins has 20 touchdown passes, and Bowers has six touchdown catches as his top target. The board makes Seattle more likely to score first, with the visible Seahawks (Smith-Njigba, Charbonnet and Jadarian Price) at roughly 44.4% against 33.2% for the visible Raiders (Bowers, Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr.), before the sportsbook’s margin. But Las Vegas has been the better scoring team this season, and Bowers at +625 gets you most of Smith-Njigba’s chance at a better price. If you think Kubiak’s knowledge of Seattle’s defense gives the Raiders an edge early, Bowers is the alternative to Smith-Njigba. First and anytime touchdown scorer odds Jaxon Smith-Njigba Zach Charbonnet Jadarian Price Ashton Jeanty Mike Washington Jr. Jeanty’s +800 is long for a back drafted sixth overall a year ago. NFL.com lists him at 362 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown this season, which goes a long way toward explaining the price. Washington’s presence on the board points to a Las Vegas backfield that is more of a split than Jeanty’s draft position suggested. Kirk Cousins passing yards Bet365’s passing yardage ladder has Cousins at -165 to reach 225 yards (roughly 62.3%) and +115 to reach 250 (roughly 46.5%). His last five games came in at 243, 313, 295, 247 and 216. He cleared 225 in four of them and 250 in two. Las Vegas ranks 30th in time of possession, so its drives tend to be short and pass-heavy, and that supports the 225 line. Same Game Parlays on the board Bet365’s featured Same Game Parlays for this game: Four Score (+1900, $10 pays $200): Zach Charbonnet, Ashton Jeanty, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Brock Bowers each to score a TD End Zone Encore (+2800, $10 pays $290): Jadarian Price, Mike Washington Jr. and Cooper Kupp each to score a TD Four Score takes the top two names from each side and needs a game with plenty of touchdowns, which sits awkwardly with a 43.5 total. End Zone Encore is the long-shot version built from secondary options. Kupp doesn’t appear among the six visible names on the touchdown scorer board. Seahawks vs. Raiders prediction and best bet A spread that moves from 7 to 3.5 usually means one of two things: new injury information or a market that decided the opener was wrong. Either way, the value on the Raiders side has mostly been taken. At +3.5 for -115, Las Vegas needs to cover about 53.5% of the time, and it has gone 1-4 in its last five. The total looks more interesting. The market has 43.5 points, and the Under is the more expensive side. The season numbers point the other way. Las Vegas averages 26.4 points and Seattle 22.4, and Cousins has passed for more than 240 yards in four of his last five games. The Raiders rank 30th in time of possession, so their drives are short, which tends to give both offenses more possessions. Kubiak also knows Seattle’s personnel from last season, and that should help Las Vegas’s offense more than its defense. The counterargument is Seattle’s defense, which ranks fourth in interceptions, and a Seahawks offense that sits 17th in yards per game. If Seattle controls the clock and Cousins throws into coverage, this can stay in the low 40s. Even so, the scoring averages and the quarterback numbers support the Over more than the Under. Best bet: Over 43.5 (-105) at Bet365 For the prop, Smith-Njigba at +425 is a better price than last week for the same role. If you would rather not need him to open the scoring, his -130 anytime price at Bet365 is the steadier route. away.headline: ‘They Didn’t Have To Tell Us That,’ ‘Definitely Unusual’ — NFL Analyst Questions Seahawks’ Decision To Reveal Sam Darnold’s Surprise Injury
away.blurb: The Seattle Seahawks will be without Sam Darnold for their Week 9 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals, but the timing of the team’s announcement seems questionable to some, especially given its decision to disclose the quarterback’s injuries. “So they got a lot of faith in Drew Lock. I just think that this idea that Wednesday, out of the blue, they tell us that Sam Darnold is out with a quad injury. They tell us that he’s week to week, which usually means you’re going to miss a couple of weeks. They didn’t have to tell us that,” Florio said. “Now I appreciate the transparency, because what they could have done, they could have just put him down as did not practice. They could have done that yesterday. They could have done it today. They could have done it tomorrow, and then they could have called him out on Friday,” the analyst continued. Drew Lock is expected to start against Arizona, although his availability for Seattle is not settled. The veteran is managing a right-elbow injury and was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated injury report after Seattle held a walkthrough. Darnold, meanwhile, is considered week-to-week and has not been placed on injured reserve. The cracked rib could potentially be managed while playing, but the quad injury is expected to keep him out against Arizona. Coach Mike Macdonald confirmed Wednesday that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game because of a quad injury suffered late in Seattle’s 34-17 loss to the Chicago Bears. Mike Florio Questions Seahawks’ Decision To Announce Sam Darnold’s Absence Early While the coach disclosed the injury, Macdonald also revealed that the quarterback had played through a cracked rib for nearly the entire game. Darnold suffered the injury on the second play against Chicago after taking a hard hit from blitzing cornerback Kyler Gordon. He did not report the issue to the coaching or medical staff during the game and continued playing through the final whistle. He finished with two touchdown passes despite the injury, and Seattle’s coaches and medical staff did not learn about the cracked rib until after the game. The decision to reveal the extent of Darnold’s injuries, however, prompted NFL analyst Mike Florio to question why Seattle chose to announce the quarterback’s absence on Wednesday rather than wait until later in the week. Speaking on “NFL on NBC” with Chris Simms, Florio said the Seahawks could have followed the league’s injury reporting rules without immediately confirming that Darnold would miss Sunday’s game. “But they decided to just lead with their chin on this, which I thought was strange. It’s definitely unusual, and it forfeits the uncertainty that the Cardinals would have as to who they’re getting ready for. Now they know they’re getting ready for Drew Lock or Jalen Milroe,” Florio added. away.headline: Sam Darnold, Drew Lock Injury Updates Provided by Seahawks HC Ahead of Raiders Game
away.blurb: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has been ruled out for Week 10 against the Las Vegas Raiders, head coach Mike Macdonald said on Monday. ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that "Darnold could attempt to try to return for next Sunday's game in Las Vegas, but the Seahawks also know that they have their bye the following week. By missing the next two games, Darnold could get the chance to rest the next three weeks before the Seahawks play a big divisional Week 12 game in San Francisco against the 49ers." Macdonald clarified it was the quad injury, not the cracked rib, keeping Darnold out of Week 9 action. The Seahawks first listed Lock on the injury report as limited with a right forearm issue ahead of a Week 6 loss at the Denver Broncos. Lock was listed as limited with a right elbow injury the following week before he was ruled out of a Week 7 win over the visiting Kansas City Chiefs. Meanwhile, backup Drew Lock appeared to get good news as looks to recover from an oblique injury suffered on Sunday: Lock went 19-of-28 for 175 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions in a 17-3 win over the Arizona Cardinals in Week 9. Darnold has been considered week-to-week but won't be placed on IR, according to Macdonald. Darnold cracked a rib on the second play of a Nov. 2 loss to the Chicago Bears before suffering the quad injury late in the game, according to Macdonald. Lock had been previously been dealing with an elbow injury but played this past week with Jalen Milroe backing him up against the Cardinals. Darnold has started seven games for the Seahawks this season, completing 60.2 percent of his passes with 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns alongside nine interceptions. Lock started in Weeks 2 and 3 after Darnold suffered a glute injury in his team's season opener. He most recently served as the Seahawks' emergency third quarterback against the Bears while Milroe backed up Darnold. Macdonald said after the Oct. 25 game the Seahawks didn't yet know the severity of Lock's injury but that it was "best for us right now to try to calm it down the best we can." Milroe has yet to see game action this season. He took just three snaps across three different contests during his rookie campaign with the Seahawks. The Seahawks (5-4) are currently deadlocked with the Los Angeles Rams for second in the NFC West behind the San Francisco 49ers (7-1).

away.headline: Seattle Seahawks Get Great Rashid Shaheed News Before Raiders Game
away.blurb: Shaheed's return is not official, but practicing without limitations to begin the week puts him in a considerably better position than he was entering Seattle's 17-3 victory over the Arizona Cardinals on November 8. Rashid Shaheed Takes Major Step Toward Seahawks Return Shaheed has been sidelined for two consecutive games, leaving Seattle without one of its most explosive offensive weapons and an important contributor in the return game. His full participation Wednesday marks a substantial improvement from last week, when he remained out of practice before ultimately being ruled out against Arizona. Having Shaheed available would give Lock another dangerous option in the passing game and provide Seattle with additional flexibility on special teams. Shaheed's possible return also comes after rookie running back Jadarian Price handled kickoff-return responsibilities against Arizona while Seattle was dealing with injuries. There is still an important distinction between returning to practice and being cleared for a game. Shaheed must make it through the remainder of the week, but Wednesday's report offered the clearest positive indication yet that he is progressing toward a return. Seattle received another encouraging update on outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu, who participated on a limited basis after also missing the past two games with an ankle injury. The situation is more concerning for Seattle's offensive line, where Cross and Nelson remain sidelined. Macdonald has already ruled Nelson out for Sunday after the veteran guard underwent a minor knee procedure earlier this week. “I'd say we haven't ruled anybody out yet, but I think everybody needs to make progress,” Macdonald said, according to Seahawks.com . Meanwhile, Lock was limited Wednesday with right elbow and oblique injuries. The quarterback suffered the oblique injury during the Cardinals game after entering the matchup with an existing elbow issue. Macdonald nevertheless expects Lock to start against Las Vegas, with Darnold targeting a possible return following Seattle's Week 11 bye. Matthew Stafford has been directing the offense, and the Rams need him to make good decisions against Arizona’s defense. away.headline: New NFL Trade Rumors on Rams' Ladd McConkey Pursuit Amid Puka Nacua, Davante Adams Injuries
away.blurb: Fowler added the Rams ultimately "didn't seriously consider a receiver move" because the team expects Matthew Stafford to succeed in the short term before Nacua and Adams return later this season. Adams has not played since rupturing his hamstring Oct. 18. Fowler reported at the time Adams hoped to return "as close to the post-Week 11 bye as possible." The Rams have also yet a few weeks to determine the future of Terrance Ferguson, who suffered a hamstring strain during his 21-day return-to-practice window on his way to coming back from an ankle injury. He must return by the end of that three-week stretch or sit out the rest of the season. The Rams have a Sunday road game against the Arizona Cardinals coming up before sitting out a Week 11 bye. McVay will hope a wide receiver room currently led by Tutu Atwell and Konata Mumpfield can keep this team afloat until Adams and Nacua are able to return in what his team hopes will be the near future. Bleacher Report • 7h Steph Ruled out vs. Rockets Justin Herbert reportedly wasn't the only player about whom the winless Los Angeles Chargers rebuffed trade inquiries ahead of Tuesday's deadline. The Los Angeles Rams are believed to have asked after wide receiver Ladd McConkey following the injuries that have sidelined Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Wednesday. "The Chargers said no to at least one Ladd McConkey inquiry," Fowler reported. "Teams I spoke to believe the Rams were the ones to make that call." Rams to Consider Trade After Puka Injury The news comes after NFL insider Jordan Schultz reported the Minnesota Vikings expressed interest in trading for Herbert before the Chargers "immediately shut down all inquiries." McConkey, who is under contract through 2027, has gone from serving as Herbert's top target last season to recording just 17 catches with 286 yards and a touchdown in six games with the struggling Chargers' offense. He missed his second game of the season last Sunday after suffering back spasms ahead of kickoff against the Houston Texans. The Rams still might have hoped a fresh start for McConkey would help the wide receiver would help add some depth around Stafford in a campaign during which he has yet to play up to his 2025 MVP form. Nacua could be hoping for a similar timeline given that the wide receiver has not yet been placed on injured reserve, although Rams coach Sean McVay has said the team expects to lose him for at least a month with an MCL and PCL sprain as well as turf toe in his right leg. away.headline: Rams Week 9 Injury Status: Myles Garrett set to return vs Washington; secondary depth hit
away.source: The Times of India on MSN
away.blurb: Los Angeles’ newly traded edge defender, Myles Garrett, has been out since Week 2 after arthroscopic surgery in mid-September. He has no injury designation for the Week 9 matchup against the Washington Commanders on Nov. 8. The Texas A&M alum practiced in a limited capacity on Wednesday and Thursday but not Friday. The Washington alum suffered a back injury while making a tackle during a Week 8 game victory over the Los Angeles Chargers. The 26-year-old cornerback did not practice all week. He is still listed as questionable for Week 9. He may be a game-time decision - probably depending on how he feels this Saturday, Nov. 7. The re-aggravation of his right shoulder dislocation ended his 2026 season. He did not practice all week. He is listed as out for Week 9. ​The 2025 draft pick was expected to be activated from injured reserve this Saturday, Nov. 7, and return to the lineup. But a brand new hamstring injury has complicated the matter. Rams wide receiver Davante Adams has been out for several weeks with a hamstring injury; if Ferguson had joined the lineup for Los Angeles quarterback Matthew Stafford in Week 9 vs. Washington, it would have helped. But the Oregon product is listed as out in the final Los Angeles Rams injury report. Grant Stuard and Kam Curl are questionable, Joe Cardona is doubtful Kam Curl suffered a foot injury, likely sustained during the Rams’ Week 8 win over the Chargers, as per RotoWire. The safety did not practice Wednesday or Thursday, but he participated in a limited capacity Friday. He is listed as questionable for the Week 9 game vs. Washington. Long snapper Joe Cardona did not practice all week due to an ankle injury he suffered in Week 7 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders. He did not play in the Week 8 vs. Chargers. He is listed as doubtful for the Week 9 game. Jake McQuaide is expected to step in from the practice squad to handle long snapping duties. The Los Angeles Rams are the third-most-injured NFL team of the 2026 season, according to the StickToTheModel injury tracker through Week 8. Get breaking news anytime, anywhere. Download the TOI app now! The star pass rusher is expected to play in Sunday’s matchup at Northwest Stadium in Landover, Maryland, at 1:00 P.M. ET. This will be his second game of the 2026 season and his second appearance for the Rams. He played 39 snaps in the Week 1 season opener against the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia. Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson injury update Jaylen Watson is also a fellow companion of Trent McDuffie coming from the Chiefs this offseason. He signed with the Rams as a free agent. The 28-year-old cornerback suffered a dislocated right shoulder in Week 3 loss against the Denver Broncos. He missed the following Week 4 win over the Philadelphia Eagles. But he returned in Week 5 and played through pain before it finally caught up with him during the Week 8 win over the Chargers. away.headline: Matthew (Stafford) has not seen the field well — Rams QB's ex-teammate calls for Los Angeles to make a trade after Puka Nacua's injury
away.blurb: Nacua’s MRI revealed MCL and PCL sprains in his right knee along with turf toe. McVay said Monday that the Rams expect Nacua to land on injured reserve, although he did not provide a specific timetable for his return. On Sunday, roughly two-thirds of Stafford’s passing yards went to one player. The Rams should have more ways to move the chains on third-and-11 than waiting for Nacua to get open again, especially if he is not going to be available for the immediate future. Puka Nacua had already caught 14 passes, piled up 150 receiving yards, and scored the go-ahead touchdown when the Los Angeles Rams gave him the ball one more time. He gained five yards on the ground and hurt his right knee on Los Angeles’ final offensive snap. The Rams left Washington with a 20-13 win and another major injury problem at wide receiver. Dan Orlovsky, Matthew Stafford’s former backup in Detroit, would have been shopping for a receiver before that handoff. With Davante Adams already on injured reserve and the trade deadline a day away, the ESPN analyst wants the Rams to make a move. Dan Orlovsky Questions Matthew Stafford’s Reads Against Washington Nacua’s injury has only added urgency after an MRI revealed MCL and PCL sprains in his right knee along with turf toe, with Sean McVay saying Monday that Nacua is expected to land on injured reserve. “Matthew has not seen the field well this year,” Orlovsky said on “The Pat McAfee Show.” “It showed up again yesterday. There’s four or five clips where I’m like, he’s just not seeing it,” Orlovsky added. “It is very Puka-centric, and they’re slow starting on offense right now. I absolutely believe that they have to be active in the wide receiver market. Absolutely. Whether Puka’s healthy or not.” For The Latest Information: NFL Injury Report Orlovsky’s comments came before it was revealed that Nacua is expected to be placed on injured reserve. Stafford completed 26 of 43 passes for 228 yards, one touchdown and one interception. He has a 76.6 PFN QB Impact Score after Week 9, which ranks 15th in the league. The Rams opened 0-for-9 on third down, and Nacua drew 19 targets. On the drive that put Los Angeles ahead for good, Stafford found him for 19 yards on third-and-11, then went back to him five plays later for the seven-yard touchdown. Orlovsky liked the run game and the tight ends. The opening drive of the second half showed what Sean McVay could do with both. Blake Corum gained 28 yards on three consecutive carries, Tyler Higbee caught a 13-yard pass and Corum finished the drive from the 1. That was a good stretch for the offense. On the biggest passing down of the fourth quarter, Stafford still needed Nacua to keep the drive alive. The defense gave the Rams time to find their footing. Myles Garrett recorded three sacks in his first game back since Week 1, including a 12-yard loss in the fourth quarter after Washington had crossed midfield. The Commanders turned the ball over on downs one play later. Puka Nacua’s Knee Injur

away.headline: Rams HC gives promising update on injured WR Davante Adams
away.blurb: McVay told reporters on Wednesday that Adams could return after the Rams Week 12 matchup against the Green Bay Packers. “We’re optimistic Davante’s return is sooner than later, which is a big deal to us,” McVay said via Myles Simmons of Pro Football Talk . If Rams fans are wondering why Adams can’t return right after their Week 11 bye, it is due to the technicalities of injured reserve. It’s safe to say the Rams will be counting down the seconds until Adams can return, though. Before suffering his hamstring injury, Adams recorded 30 catches for 480 yards and four touchdowns. The Los Angeles Rams once had one of the most feared wide receiver rooms in the NFL , but that has quickly changed after watching star wide receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams become sidelined injuries. Rams head coach Sean McVay recently revealed the offense may not be without Adams for too much longer, though. That is certainly good news, given the state of the Rams wide receiver room. With Nacua and Adams sidelined and the team’s decision to not add another playmaker at the NFL’s trade deadline, Los Angeles is now forced to rely on the likes of Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, CJ Daniels and Xavier Smith. That could bode bad news for the Rams as they continue to fall further behind in a competitive NFC West. The San Fransisco 49ers currently sit atop the division at 6-1 while the Seattle Seahawks are in second place at 5-4. Los Angeles placed Adams on injured reserve after suffering a ruptured hamstring tendon during its Week 7 loss to the Arizona Cardinals. Since bye weeks do not count toward games spent on injured reserve, Adams must remain sidelined through Week 12 to meet his minimum four games. A second-round pick in the 2014 NFL Draft by the Packers, Adams has recorded 1,047 catches for 13,113 yards and 121 touchdowns in his professional career. The Rams are scheduled to have their rematch against the Cardinals in Week 10. home.headline: Cardinals QB situation takes stunning turn with Gardner Minshew update: report
home.blurb: Following their 17-3 road loss Sunday to the Seattle Seahawks, the Arizona Cardinals received a major update on quarterback Gardner Minshew, who may have suffered a season-ending injury. On Monday evening, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that Minshew “is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm.” Rapoport said Minshew suffered the injury before halftime but continued playing through it. According to Rapoport, Minshew will get additional testing done, but the injury could end his season and require a lengthy rehabilitation process. Minshew suffered the injury when he was hit by Seahawks pass rusher Dante Fowler while attempting a pass on the final play of the first half. The Cardinals quarterback grabbed his right arm after the rough hit, but continued to play. In Sunday’s game, Minshew completed 21 of 30 passes for 166 yards and was sacked three times by the Seahawks defense. Seattle held Arizona to just 198 total yards of offense for the game. More news: Chiefs HC Andy Reid Reveals Patrick Mahomes Injury Update Ahead of Falcons Game The devastating update arrived days after the team traded veteran starter Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens. Arizona’s unfortunate situation with Minshew has led to several developments, including Adam Schefter reporting that the team signed Josh Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. This is Johnson’s 15th team in 14 seasons. According to ESPN , in an initial report on the Cardinals’ injury updates, rookie Carson Beck was expected to start on Sunday. The Cardinals drafted the former Miami Hurricanes quarterback at No. 65 in the 3rd round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Beck led his team to the College Football Playoff National Championship game, which they lost to Fernando Mendoza and the Indiana Hoosiers. The decision to draft Beck was met with mixed reviews, with many sports outlets giving the team a low grade for the pick. NFL.com’s Chad Reuter graded Arizona’s Day 2 picks, including Beck, an “A,” indicating he had “a lot of big-game experience.” However, Reuter also noted that Beck’s decision-making was too inconsistent to be a “surefire starter.” Beck appeared in the NFL Hall of Fame Game this preseason against the Carolina Panthers, throwing for 188 yards and a touchdown in Arizona’s 33-30 loss. With ESPN reporting that Beck is expected to start Sunday, he’s poised to take over for a 3-6 Arizona team, unless they opt to use Johnson instead. Unfortunately, both quarterbacks could face a challenging matchup for the team’s next NFL game. The Cardinals host a Los Angeles Rams team on Sunday, Nov. 15, that has now won three straight games to improve to 5-4 for the season. The Rams also just got back the NFL Defensive Player of the Year, Myles Garrett, who recorded three sacks on Sunday in their 20-13 win over the Washington Commanders, so Beck or Johnson could face a difficult test for his first NFL start. home.headline: Just how bad are Cardinals injuries? See where they rank
home.blurb: To be fair, the Cardinals’ injuries are largely limited to the offensive side of the ball. Cornerback Will Johnson is out for the season with a neck injury, but he is the only defensive starter currently sidelined. And yet, he’s never seen an injury crisis quite like the one he faces in his debut season as the Arizona Cardinals head coach. “Not to this level, no,” LaFleur said. “At least in one particular position group.” So, just how bad are the Cardinals' injuries? Well, just look at their Week 1 offensive depth chart: RB: Jeremiyah Love (injured reserve) WR: Michael Wilson (injured reserve) WR: Marvin Harrison Jr. (traded) WR: Kendrick Bourne (injured reserve) LT: Paris Johnson Jr. (injured reserve) C: Hjalte Froholdt (concussion protocol) If Froholdt indeed misses this week’s game, the Cardinals would be down to just four of their Week 1 starters. Even excluding him, they’ve lost six of those top 11. The results tell the story. Over the past four weeks, the Cardinals rank a respectable 19th in points per drive allowed and 12th in yards per play allowed. It’s been their best defensive stretch in nearly two years. On the flip side, their offense ranks 24th and 28th, respectively, in those same metrics. “The defense, there's been a guy here and there, but there's been some decent continuity over the last month,” LaFleur said. “And I think you guys see that. I think you see 11 as one more and more each week, particularly over these last four weeks. Not the case on offense right now.” It’s an injury barrage that is unmatched across the league. The Cardinals’ seven offensive players on injured reserve is the most in the league, with those four aforementioned Week 1 starters joined by Gardner Minshew, Jalen Brooks and Hunter Long. Only one other team — the Los Angeles Chargers — even has six offensive players on IR. League average is 2.7. When looking only at offensive starters, the story is similar, as the Cardinals lead the league with four on IR. Only two teams — the New England Patriots and Los Angeles Rams — have three offensive starters on IR. League average is 1.2. The Cardinals’ defense, by contrast, has had slightly better health than league average. Still, just 43 of the 53 players from the Cardinals’ Week 1 squad remain on the active roster. Only the Atlanta Falcons have had more attrition. As a result, it’s difficult to assess exactly where the Cardinals roster stands. That’s not to say that their poor performances have been entirely attributable to injury — Marvin Harrison Jr., the offensive line and the pass rush have all struggled even when healthy. But any overarching assessment, at least on offense, has to account for the unwelcome wave of injuries.

home.headline: Cardinals Forced to Sign 40-Year-Old QB as Injuries Mount
home.blurb: “I think probably even stronger than how I said it yesterday. I wasn’t anticipating some of the things that we found out today. I knew that particularly on offense — (with) the defense there’s been a guy here and there, but there’s been some decent continuity over the last month, and I think you guys see that," LaFleur said. Cardinals Coach Said The Quiet Part Out Loud on Carson Beck ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals' Monday has taken a steep twist thanks to several significant injuries to their offense, and with news of Gardner Minshew potentially being done for the season, the organization has already targeted their next passer. From ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter: "With veteran QB Gardner Minshew sidelined due to a UCL injury, the Cardinals are signing QB Josh Johnson off the Bengals’ practice squad, per sources. The Cardinals will be Johnson’s 15th NFL team in 14 NFL seasons." Johnson, a perennial backup veteran quarterback, will be the team's No. 2 quarterback as the Cardinals prepare for their Week 10 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams — who just welcomed Myles Garrett back to the mix with a three-sack performance this Sunday. Minshew was injured on the final play of the second quarter against Seattle. He returned to finish the game but showed obvious discomfort. Rookie quarterback Carson Beck is slated to start for Arizona this week. Johnson, 40 years old, first entered the league as a fifth-round pick in the 2008 NFL Draft. He's played 50 NFL games with 11 starts, most recently starting twice for the Washington Commanders in 2025. In those two games, Johnson completed 34 of 54 passes for 372 yards for one touchdown and two interceptions. He has a 2-9 record as a starter. It was an extremely tough day for the Cardinals, who lost both Minshew and Michael Wilson . Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur says the team has to regroup, even amid the injuries. "I think you see 11 has won more and more each week, particularly over these last four weeks. Not the case on offense right now and that’s what I meant by that. There’s been a lot of moving parts, and I have to do a better job of stabilizing that to make sure that we don’t have performances like we did yesterday.” The Cardinals recently dealt Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens last week, thinning their quarterback room down to two. With Minshew injured, Beck was the only healthy quarterback on the roster prior to Johnson's signing. home.headline: Arizona Cardinals face quarterback crisis as Gardner Minshew faces potential season-ending injury
home.blurb: Head coach Mike LaFleur addressed the media on Monday, confirming that Minshew is scheduled for an MRI to determine the full extent of the damage. While the team has not officially ruled the quarterback out for the year, the organization is already preparing for a transition under center. Reports indicate that rookie Carson Beck is the primary candidate to assume the starting responsibilities should Minshew be placed on the sidelines for an extended period. The Arizona Cardinals are confronting a significant roster challenge following reports that starting quarterback Gardner Minshew II has sustained a torn ulnar collateral ligament (UCL) in his throwing arm. The injury, which occurred during Sunday’s game against the Seattle Seahawks, has raised concerns that the 30-year-old signal-caller may be sidelined for the remainder of the season. The incident took place on the final play of the first half when Minshew was struck while being sacked. Despite the severity of the injury, Minshew returned to the field for the third quarter and completed the game. Following the contest, NFL insider Ian Rapoport reported that the quarterback is undergoing further medical evaluations, with initial assessments suggesting a recovery period that could span several months. Transition to Rookie Leadership and Roster Adjustments Beck’s path to the starting lineup was cleared earlier this week when the Cardinals traded veteran Jacoby Brissett, effectively elevating the rookie to the backup position. Although Beck has yet to make his regular-season debut, he saw significant action during the preseason Hall of Fame Game against the Carolina Panthers, where he completed 15 of 19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown. His development was previously hindered by a rib injury, but his recent promotion has increased his involvement in team practices. To bolster the quarterback room, the Cardinals are reportedly moving to sign veteran Josh Johnson from the Cleveland Browns' practice squad. The addition of Johnson provides the team with necessary depth as they navigate the uncertainty surrounding Minshew’s status and prepare for the upcoming stretch of the season. Live Simms Unbuttoned Brian Hamilton , Brian Hamilton At one time…a few decades ago…the 49ers and the Cowboys was the top rivalry in the NFL. In 2026, Sunday’s game between the 49ers (7-1) and the Cowboys (4-5) features one team contending for a Super Bowl and the other simply battling to remain in contention in an underwhelming division. The contrast extends beyond the standings is explained in the numbers: the 49ers are averaging 29.4 points per game while allowing 19.5, compared with 27.3 scored and 26.2 allowed by the Cowboys. San Francisco arrives in Arlington following a convincing 38-17 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, a game the 49ers broke open with a turnover-fueled second half. Brock Purdy completed 17 of 25 passes for 232 yards and two touchdowns and also ran for a score, while Christian McCaffrey scored once on the ground and once through the air. San Francisco led 21-10 at halftime before Jaden Dugger returned an interception 35 yards for a touchdown on the Raiders’ first offensive play of the third quarter. That started a remarkable half in which the 49ers forced five turnovers. The Niners finished with 414 total yards, including 190 rushing, possessed the ball for more than 38 minutes. Dallas also enters the matchup following a victory, escaping Indianapolis with a 27-23 win over the Colts after trailing 23-20 with less than two minutes remaining. Dak Prescott immediately answered with a 46-yard completion to Ryan Flournoy , and Javonte Williams scored from one yard out with 1:08 remaining to put Dallas ahead for good. The Cowboys piled up 508 yards of offense to Indianapolis’ 271, with Prescott completing 21 of 34 passes for 335 yards and two touchdowns, CeeDee Lamb exploding for 10 catches and 195 yards and a score, and Williams rushing for 101 yards. But Dallas made life difficult for itself with two turnovers and 14 penalties for 153 yards. This is a rivalry that has produced some of the most memorable postseason games in NFL history, from “The Catch” in the 1981 NFC Championship Game to three consecutive NFC title-game meetings between the clubs following the 1992, 1993 and 1994 seasons. San Francisco currently owns the upper hand, leading the all-time series 21-19-1 and having won the past four meetings, including playoff victories of 23-17 after the 2021 season and 19-12 after the 2022 season. The 49ers followed those wins with a 42-10 rout in 2023 and a 30-24 victory in the most recent meeting on Oct. 27, 2024. home.blurb: Brian Schottenheimer told reporters, including Joseph Hoyt of The Dallas Morning News , that George Pickens and Joey Porter Jr., along with two other key players, are set to return to practice prior to Week 10. Dak Prescott could really use Pickens back in the lineup. With Jake Ferguson hurt, the Cowboys' passing offense is funneling through CeeDee Lamb and Ryan Flournoy. Pickens' return would open things up for everyone involved. Dallas won't be out of the playoff hunt if they lose in Week 10, but a victory would have them in great shape to make a second-half run to the playoffs. Getting Pickens, Porter, Overshown, and Turpin back would be a huge help. home.headline: Cowboys injury report: Overshown’s latest setback, Pickens and Porter Jr. updates
home.blurb: But the Cowboys won't be going into this game fully staffed either. Earlier this week, fans learned that Malachi Lawrence would be out for several weeks with an ankle injury, but he's not the only one in danger of missing this weekend's contest. Let's check out the latest regarding DeMarvion Overshown, George Pickens, Joey Porter Jr., Caleb Downs and others. On Friday, Schotteheimer told 105.3 The Fan that they needed to "get him out there today and see how he does.” Overshown is questionable after being limited the last two days. It always seems to be something with him, unfortunately, so fans won't hold their breath for Overshown to be active. Pickens has been dealing with a multitude of injuries this year, it seems, which at least partially explains his downturn in production. He was limited in all three practices leading up to the Colts game, and he is also questionable for Sunday. Dallas knew Porter Jr. was not 100% upon his arrival, but he's been a mainstay on the injury report and a full-on question mark every week, it feels like. He was full on Wednesday but has been limited the last two days, which is a bit worrisome, but Porter Jr. is questionable for Week 9. Schottenheimer said before Friday's practice that he was "hopeful" to have both Pickens and Porter Jr. against Indianapolis. Fans will find out Sunday morning if that was just wishful thinking. After missing the last two-plus games, Dee Winters will return for Dallas. The Cowboys have not had a fully healthy linebacker corps for an entire game this season, and if Overshown misses Sunday, it will remain that way. But for the time being, he is at least insurance if Overshown is out. Jake Ferguson improved from a non-participant on Wednesday and Thursday to being limited on Friday. It remains to be seen if he can play through his ankle injury, but he is officially questionable. Of course, Malachi Lawrence is out with the aforementioned ankle injury, and Kavontae Turpin will miss his third straight game with an injury to his ribs. Jonathan Bullard and Marist Liufau have not been activated to the 53-man roster, but they both practiced in full all week. Officially, they are questionable as the Cowboys mull over their roster math equations. Rapid fire: Luke Schoonmaker is questionable. Tyler Smith and Kenny Clark are good to go. The Dallas Cowboys' season already feels like it is on the ropes in Week 9 as they travel to take on one of the only teams in the NFL that are spiraling worse than they are: the Indianapolis Colts. And this is a get-right game if I've ever seen one, or if that even matters for Brian Schottenheimer's team. Indianapolis has already sold off great veterans like Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, and word on the street is that Josh Downs and Jonathan Taylor, and maybe more, could be next. The vibes are certainly low in the Colts' locker room, and some "business decisions" could be made on Sunday. Dallas Cowboys injury update before Week 9 game vs. Indianapolis Colts

home.headline: Cowboys Injury Roundup: 'Tough decisions' ahead as Ferguson, Locke, others get bad news
home.blurb: FRISCO, Texas — Roughly two weeks ago, the Dallas Cowboys were feeling great about their injury report as key players began to get healthy and return to the practice and playing field. In the blink of an eye, they're suddenly back to having a lengthy and growing list of injuries that will again cost them impact players going forward. PJ Locke missed time this season before returning and suffering a concussion in Week 8, clearing protocol ahead of the matchup against the Indianapolis Colts before suffering a second concussion in as many weeks and, this time, he will not return in only a week's time. On Monday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer and the Cowboys officially ruled Locke out of the looming contest against the San Francisco 49ers — a sign he will likely miss multiple games. It was a scary sight to see Locke lying motionless for several moments before being helped to the sideline and not being permitted to return at Lucas Oil Stadium. Turpin will join DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring/back), George Pickens (hamstring) and Joey Porter Jr. (ankle), those three were ruled out ahead of kickoff against the Colts, in the rehab group this week to determine if either of them can go against the 49ers. And with Ferguson down, the expectation is that Luke Schoonmaker will return from injury to help with the currently ailing tight end depth chart. And though Marist Liufau was activated from injured reserve last week, Malachi Lawrence recently joined Thompson on IR, leaving the Cowboys with only one IR-DTR (designated to return) spot this regular season, assuming Lawrence returns as expected. That means if Ferguson, Goodson and Locke are moved to IR, only one of them would be allowed to return unless the Cowboys make the playoffs. On the day of the NFL's trade deadline, Cowboys owner/GM Jerry Jones said on 105.3 The Fan that he is not expecting Dallas to make a significant trade, "but don't count it out." In pulling out a much-needed win in Indianapolis, the Cowboys seemingly took craziness to a whole new level. After challenging his defense to execute for a full 60 minutes, Quinnen Williams led by example with a dominant performance that helped the Cowboys finish strong and close out a crucial victory. (USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect) In this article George Pickens, KaVontae Turpin Limited At Cowboys Practice Joey Porter Jr. Sits After A Limited Finish Last Week FRISCO, Texas — Tight end Jake Ferguson and running back Tyler Goodson did not practice Wednesday as the Dallas Cowboys opened their week of preparation for the San Francisco 49ers . Both are listed with knee and ankle injuries on the Cowboys’ practice report. Both players suffered knee injuries Sunday in Dallas’ 27-23 win over the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium. Ferguson caught the Cowboys’ first touchdown of the afternoon before a later hit knocked him out of the game. Goodson ran for 77 yards on 6.4 yards per carry and handled kick returns with KaVontae Turpin sidelined. On Monday, Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said both players would miss multiple weeks. Eight players in all sat out Wednesday. Edge rusher Donovan Ezeiruaku (ankle), wide receiver Jonathan Mingo (ankle), cornerback Joey Porter Jr. (ankle), and safety P.J. Locke (concussion) joined Ferguson and Goodson. Safety Malik Hooker was excused for a personal matter, and outside linebacker Von Miller received a rest day. George Pickens, KaVontae Turpin Limited At Cowboys Practice Three players were limited. Wide receivers George Pickens (hamstring) and Turpin (ribs) both took part on a limited basis, as did linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring, back). Pickens and Overshown both missed the Colts game, and Porter did too. Ezeiruaku sprained his ankle against Indianapolis, and the team considers him day-to-day. Locke suffered his second concussion in as many weeks at Lucas Oil Stadium, and Dallas ruled him out for Sunday on Monday. Safety Jalen Thompson remains out after missing seven games with a hamstring injury. Porter opened last week with a full practice, was limited Thursday, and then sat out Sunday’s game in Indianapolis. Dallas acquired the cornerback from the Pittsburgh Steelers in an October trade. picks.headline: ‘Bring your popcorn’- Mike Tomlin makes bold prediction for Steelers-Bengals clash
picks.blurb: ‘Bring your popcorn’- Mike Tomlin makes bold prediction for Steelers-Bengals clash - Yahoo Sports Search query for Search Search News Finance More Mail NFL Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images Aryan Chadha · HITC Mon, 9 November 2026 at 11:30 am UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Premier League Scottish Football Champions League Europa League Club World Cup About our ads Mike Tomlin is expecting a blockbuster AFC North showdown between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals, backing both teams to deliver an entertaining contest with the division lead at stake. The former Steelers head coach knows exactly what this rivalry means after spending 19 years in Pittsburgh before stepping away from the role. He will now get to watch his old team from the NBC crew as the two sides prepare to meet on Sunday Night Football. Both teams enter the contest with 6-2 records and four consecutive victories, setting up a major meeting between two sides looking to strengthen their position in the AFC North. Mike Tomlin backs Steelers pass rush to challenge Joe Burrow and Cincinnati Bengals Tomlin made no secret of his excitement when discussing the matchup, admitting he would be more than happy to make the trip to Cincinnati. "It's AFC North football and you know I love that. You can airmail me right to Cincinnati," Tomlin said. He also highlighted the individual battle that could define the game, with Joe Burrow and the Bengals passing attack facing Pittsburgh's formidable pass rush. "It's good on good. Joe Burrow and that Cincinnati passing game vs T.J. Watt and the four-man rush of the Steelers…. Bring your popcorn and get your cameras ready." Pittsburgh will arrive with plenty of confidence after enjoying a bye week. The Steelers' four-game winning run includes a commanding 27-6 victory over the Cleveland Browns in their most recent outing. Cincinnati have also found their rhythm, beating the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid. Burrow completed 82.8 per cent of his passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in that victory. However, the Bengals will have revenge on their minds after losing 30-27 to Pittsburgh during their earlier meeting this season. That defeat came during a difficult spell in which Cincinnati also suffered a second consecutive loss. Now, with both teams level at 6-2, the stakes are considerably higher. Tomlin will have a particularly interesting perspective from the NBC booth as he watches the Steelers take on a Bengals team that will be determined to settle the score on home turf. picks.headline: Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final
picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Power Rankings Fantasy Football NFL news, live updates Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs NFL midseason awards Rex Ryan arrested Skubal suitors emerge Bengals vs. Steelers predictions: Joe Burrow, Jaylen Warren and a 34-31 final (Sam Greene/The Enquirer / USA TODAY) Keegan Nickoson · Roundtable Sports Wed, November 11, 2026 at 11:53 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Joe Burrow accounts for four touchdowns for the fifth straight game Burrow is on a heater, scoring four or more touchdowns, whether throwing or running, in four straight games. In his last four games against the Steelers, Burrow has thrown 11 touchdowns and four interceptions, topping 275 yards in all four games. Interestingly, Pittsburgh is a great matchup for Burrow. The Steelers play zone coverage on 84.3% of dropbacks, according to Next Gen Stats, and Burrow is the best quarterback in the NFL against zone by completion percentage, at 74.7%. Jaylen Warren rushes for 120-plus yards Warren has become one of the league's most productive running backs this season, ranking sixth in rushing yards and first in yards per carry, at 5.9. Earlier this season against the Bengals , Warren ran for the second-most yards of his season, with 127. Two weeks ago against Cleveland, Warren topped that number with 143 yards. It was the first time all season he rushed for 100 yards in back-to-back games. The Bengals' defense has been inconsistent this season, struggling with tackling some weeks and shutting down opposing offenses and forcing takeaways in others. I think that, coming off a bye, the Steelers catch the Bengals on their back foot and feed Warren, who will have a big game. Steelers win 34-31 History is not on the Bengals' side in this matchup. After playing an overseas game, teams are 0-5 when their next game comes against a team coming off a bye. The Steelers are rested, while the Bengals are recovering from nearly a full week in Madrid. A lot is at stake in this game, with the winner taking sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Pittsburgh doesn't have much momentum, especially on offense, as its best wide receiver, DK Metcalf, has been struggling with drops lately. He has just 378 receiving yards this season and has topped 100 yards just once, with a 115-yard day against Cleveland earlier this season. Metcalf had just one catch for 4 yards on six targets against the Browns. The Steelers hit a snag at the right time, giving themselves a week to figure things out. I think the Steelers pick up a big win, halting the Bengals' momentum and getting a massive tiebreaker. Pittsburgh has done a relatively good job of keeping a cap on Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins over the last couple of seasons. Outside of Chase's massive 16-catch, 161-yard game with Joe Flacco at quarterback last season, neither has topped 100 yards in their last four meetings.

away.headline: Steelers Week 10 Injury Report: Derrick Harmon Returns to Practice Ahead of Bengals Showdown
away.blurb: Pittsburgh is dealing with several injuries, though many of those players got an extra week of rest during the bye. Now the Steelers need to see who is trending toward being available, including a few players eligible to come off injured reserve. Will any of them start working their way back this week? Practice designations: FP: Full Participation | LP: Limited Participation | DNP: Did Not Participate The Steelers got huge news this week: defensive tackle Harmon’s 21-day practice window is open. Harmon went on injured reserve after suffering a foot injury in Week 4 and has missed four games. He is now eligible to return and could be activated as soon as this week. Safety Elliott was the other limited participant, with an ankle injury. He’s one to watch over the next few days as he works his way back into a bigger role on defense. The only Steelers who missed practice were Watt, Heyward and Washington, who all took rest days. Wide receiver Skowronek could return from his Week 5 injury to a receiver room that is already thin. He has good chemistry with quarterback Aaron Rodgers and is a valuable special teams player. Cornerbacks Echols and Slaughter also practiced fully, which is more good news for Pittsburgh. Both are key special teams contributors, and their ability to play in the slot and on the outside makes them welcome depth at cornerback. The Pittsburgh Steelers head to Cincinnati in Week 10 for a game with real AFC North stakes against the Bengals . The winner takes first place in the division with eight games left in the season. Pittsburgh won the first meeting in Week 3, and this grudge match gives the Steelers a chance to sweep Cincinnati for the first time since 2023. Doing so would go a long way toward repeating as AFC North champions. Here is the Steelers’ first injury report as they prepare for their road trip to Cincinnati. away.headline: Pittsburgh Steelers fans might be disappointed, but Mike McCarthy isn’t worried about missing the trade deadline
away.blurb: Pittsburgh Steelers fans might be disappointed, but Mike McCarthy isn’t worried about missing the trade deadline - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs Nick Farabaugh · PennLive.com Wed, November 11, 2026 at 9:19 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers did not end up making any big moves at the trade deadline, and that was not much of a surprise. With the team standing pat, however, head coach Mike McCarthy says he is happy with his wide receiver room. If the Steelers were going to trade for a player, it likely would have been at the wide receiver position. "I feel great about our guys. I mean, we're getting guys healthy. Michael [Pittman Jr.] is getting close, obviously, Roman [Wilson] and Max [Hurleman]. So, we've got good young guys. Both the Brandons [Smith and Johnson]. So, we've got a group that I'm excited to continue to work with," McCarthy said. McCarthy was not as involved in the decision-making process for trades as general manager Omar Khan. In the past, head coach Mike Tomlin had been heavily involved in the decisions being made on the roster. While McCarthy certainly has a say in those, it seems he is not as active as some other coaches in that area of team building. "I think my individual focus is always on our current roster. I spoke on this, was it yesterday? When was the last time we talked? I think it's important, as I've learned over the years, to keep the energy there. I mean, I understand what goes on. I mean, that's what Omar [Khan] and our personnel staff is always working on, player acquisition and grading of players and that whole process.So, as far as what all went down, that's probably better-served for questions for others. I'm focused on our guys," McCarthy said. The Steelers made some additions to their roster in the post trade deadline craze a year ago. They signed Adam Thielen and Marquez Valdes-Scantling at wide receiver and brought in Asante Samuel Jr. at cornerback. Pittsburgh could still make some of those moves on the margins this year, but if they do make those types of moves, they are unlikely to be as impactful as a potential trade could have been for the team. away.headline: Steelers receive huge injury update on two starters
away.blurb: Both Pittman and Harmon are eligible to be activated off IR in time for the Week 10 matchup against the Bengals, but as McCarthy pointed out, it remains to be seen if the two Steelers will be cleared for Sunday. Steelers receive huge injury update on two starters - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Misiorowski, Schlittler win Cy Youngs Steelers receive huge injury update on two starters Andrew Vasquez, Steelers Wire · Steelers Wire Tue, November 10, 2026 at 11:06 AM UTC · 1 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy provided a huge injury update on two players currently on IR. Speaking to reporters on Monday, McCarthy revealed that although Michael Pittman Jr. and Derrick Harmon's status for the Week 10 game against the Cincinnati Bengals remains uncertain, they are "getting close" to returning to action. Pittman, who spent the first six years of his career with the Indianapolis Colts (2020-2025), was traded to the Steelers in March 2026. He re-aggravated a foot injury during Week 5 practice and was subsequently placed on injured reserve on October 10. Harmon, who was drafted by the Steelers in the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft, had a solid start to the 2026 season, recording 12 combined tackles, one tackle for loss, 1.5 sacks, and one forced fumble during the first four games of the season. He suffered his foot injury in Week 4 and was placed on injured reserve on October 5. Defensive tackle Derrick Harmon returned to practice today but remains on the Reserve/Injured List. The Steelers have a 21-day window to either activate Harmon or he remains on the Reserve/Injured List for the remainder of the season. He was placed on the Reserve/Injured List on October 10. Harmon, the Steelers No. 1 pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, appeared in four games this year, with one start, before he was placed on the Reserve/Injured List. He has 12 tackles this season, including three solo stops and a tackle for a loss. He also has one and a half sacks and a forced fumble. In two seasons, Harmon has appeared in 16 games, with nine starts. He is credited with 39 tackles, including 14 solo tackles, as well as two tackles for a loss. He also has four and a half sacks, a pass defense and a forced fumble. "I think Michael is getting close," said McCarthy on Monday. "I know his workout, I'm going to say Friday, was something that hopefully we can do more. "We just want to get our guys, get them healthy. We're going to be obviously healthier than we've been in a while. So, it will be good to see really what Wednesday gives us as far as who we think is going to be ready for Cincinnati." "I think any time you can get your full group of guys back, it certainly eliminates the stress that other guys have to do to pick up the load." home.blurb: Left guard Dylan Fairchild (pectoral), is the new name to monitor this week. Fairchild injured his pectoral late in last Sunday’s victory over the Atlanta Falcons. It caused him to miss the very last snap of the game. Coach Zac Taylor told reporters Wednesday that they’ll take Fairchild day-to-day. Being limited to start the week off is a positive sign. Cornerback DJ Turner II (heel) was also limited. There was a chance he wouldn’t play last Sunday, but he was able to Stay in the field for nearly the entire game. Cincinnati will likely take it easy with him until his ankle is fully healed. Defense end Cedric Johnson is notably not included in the injury report, A great sign that his ankle/foot Injury from last week is no longer a concern. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) aggravated his quad injury during Week 7 and is still week-to-week. Defensive tackle Jonathan Allen had his usual rest day. By George Karmpoulonis The Chargers at Ravens Monday night game in Week 10 pairs the NFL's only winless team with a Ravens side that has lost four straight. The Chargers are 0-8 and have dropped 11 consecutive games dating to last season, the franchise's longest losing streak since it started 0-11 in 2000, according to ESPN. The Ravens are 4-5 without Lamar Jackson, who is on injured reserve after thumb surgery. The game also puts Jim Harbaugh against Jesse Minter, who spent two seasons as the Chargers' defensive coordinator and two before that running Harbaugh's defense at Michigan. The Chargers allow 122 rushing yards per game and just traded starting linebacker Daiyan Henley to the Broncos, so their linebacker group is thinner than it was a week ago. A run-heavy script also suits the Ravens because the Chargers score a league-low 15.1 points per game and have not topped 23 in any of their last five. The Ravens still have to score with a quarterback who joined the team last week. They have put up 13 or fewer points in four straight games, and Jacoby Brissett's career record as a starter is 23-50, according to ESPN. Their defense has also allowed 35, 36 and 33 points in its last three games. The Ravens are 1-3 at home, so their 34-point edge in the market rests largely on the Chargers' 0-8 record and the Chargers' scoring problems. How could Chargers vs Ravens unfold? The Ravens can shorten the game by running. They gained 172 yards on the ground against Jacksonville last Thursday, including Justice Hill's 65-yard touchdown, but managed only 55 net passing yards with Joe Fagnano at quarterback. Brissett threw for 1,719 yards, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions in eight starts for Arizona before the Cardinals benched him, according to Sportsnet, so offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has a more experienced passer to pair with Henry. The Chargers need to change the shape of the game. They went 12 straight quarters and 37 offensive drives without a touchdown before Quentin Johnston's 58-yard score against Houston, according to ESPN. Omarion Hampton leads the team with 369 rushing yards, and Herbert has completed 144 of 235 passes, but his 11 interceptions lead the NFL, tied with New England's Drake Maye. Minter spent the last two seasons running the Chargers' defense and knows their staff, including coordinator Chris O'Leary, whom he mentored. That familiarity gives the Ravens a detailed read on the opposition, and the offense he now faces, run by Mike McDaniel, has produced little against anyone this season. What is the latest team news? Both teams carry questions at quarterback and in the secondary, and the statuses can change before the final injury designations arrive. What is the latest on the Chargers? Herbert is listed as questionable with an injury to the middle finger of his left, non-throwing hand. X-rays were negative, and Harbaugh said Monday that he "should be good to go." Herbert left the Texans game in the fourth quarter, and DJ Uiagalelei finished it. Wide receiver Ladd McConkey is questionable after back spasms kept him out of the Texans game. Harbaugh described him as day-to-day on Monday, according to NDTV US Sports. Cornerbacks Isas Waxter and Cam Hart and defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe all hurt ankles against Houston, and Harbaugh said the Chargers would "see how the week goes." What is the latest on the Ravens? Minter said Monday that he expects Brissett to start. Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) are on injured reserve, and Fagnano, the undrafted rookie who started against Jacksonville, has dealt with an ankle issue. Safety Kyle Hamilton is questionable with a hip injury, and Minter said he "looks fairly good." Cornerback Nate Wiggins (illness) and safety Jaylinn Hawkins (knee) are also questionable, and Minter was optimistic about both returning this week. What could decide Chargers vs Ravens? Three matchups look most likely to separate two teams that have combined for one win in their last 10 games. Can the Chargers protect Herbert? The Chargers rank 31st of 32 teams in sacks allowed with 31, and Herbert went down a career-high eight times against Houston. The Ravens have 17 sacks in nine games, led by Mike Green with 3.5, but they had just two in their last three games after sacking Cleveland five times in Week 6. If the pass rush stays quiet, Herbert gets the time his offense has lacked. Can Brissett give the Ravens a different offense? The Ravens have had 11 days since their last game and the Chargers eight, which gives Brissett more time to learn Doyle's offense. Zay Flowers leads the team with 614 receiving yards, and the Chargers allow 27.4 points per game, tied for 28th. The Chargers' defense does rank eighth in opponent third-down rate at 34.3%, so Brissett cannot count on easy conversions. Who wins the turnover battle? The Chargers have 19 giveaways, tied for 31st, and a turnover margin of minus-seven. They turned the ball over at least twice in each of their last five games. The Ravens gave it away three times in each of their last two games, so a short field is the quickest way either offense can find points. What could move Chargers vs Ravens prediction? Herbert's final designation and McConkey's availability decide how much the Chargers can threaten a Ravens secondary that allowed 280 net passing yards to Buffalo and 242 to Jacksonville. On the Ravens side, Brissett's confirmation as the starter and the status of Hamilton, Wiggins and Hawkins shape both their passing game and their coverage.
