home.headline: Lamar Jackson's Message to Ravens Revealed in NFL Rumors amid Injury, Return Buzz and Losing Streak
home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is aiming to return during the 2026 NFL season, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . After playing the first three games of the year, he missed three games because of a high ankle sprain, returning to action on Nov. 1 against the Buffalo Bills. His return was brief, however, as he suffered a thumb injury on the Ravens' first offensive drive. Rapoport reported that Jackson spoke to the team and delivered an "energizing" and "exciting" message. The overall theme was to "just stay alive" until he's healthy enough to be back on the field. The Ravens are last in the AFC North at 4-5 following Thursday's 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. The combined absences of Jackson and Tyler Huntley were glaring as third-stringer Joe Fagnano threw for 60 yards and two interceptions on 18 attempts. Jackson has unfortunately had another injury-riddled year. The injury required surgery, and the two-time MVP was placed on the injured reserve immediately after the game. Huntley came in for Jackson after his injury, but he was forced to exit soon after because of a turf toe injury. A day after the Jaguars loss, Baltimore acquired Jacoby Brissett from the Arizona Cardinals. Brissett is a significant upgrade from Fagnano and may be enough for the team to keep its head above water in the weeks ahead. It's clear Jackson isn't throwing away the rest of the season, and that attitude is bound to spread to the rest of the locker room.

home.headline: Report: Ravens QB Lamar Jackson plans to return this season
home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson told teammates that he plans to return this season shortly after suffering a right thumb injury against the Buffalo Bills last Sunday, according to a report from ESPN’s Ian Rapoport . Jackson encouraged his team to keep their playoff hopes alive until he comes back. His IR placement will sideline him until after Baltimore’s Week 13 bye; however, surgery on his throwing hand will likely sideline him for longer. Rapoport adds that Jackson is specifically dealing with a fractured and dislocated thumb that typically has a six- to nine-week recovery timeline. If that is accurate, his earliest return would be in Week 15 against the Pittsburgh Steelers, a game that will likely have significant playoff implications. Nine weeks would keep Jackson out until Week 18, the Ravens’ second matchup against the Steelers, by which time taking the field may not make sense. Jackson’s potential return will only matter if recent trade acquisition Jacoby Brissett and Baltimore’s struggling defense can keep the team in the playoff race over the next month. They will face the winless Los Angeles Chargers in Week 10, who could be without starting quarterback Justin Herbert. After that are the Houston Texans and the Carolina Panthers, two of the NFL’s Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde teams this year, followed by the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers post-bye. The Ravens probably need to win three of those games, to get to 7-6, to keep their playoff hopes alive. They would then need at least two, if not three wins over the Steelers (twice), Cleveland Browns, and Cincinnati Bengals to close the season. It’s worth noting that Jackson recently called out Rapoport for an inaccurate report that he suffered a unique, neither high nor low ankle sprain. The two-time MVP said that head athletic trainer Adrian Dixon told him that it was, in fact, a high ankle sprain. As of Saturday, Jackson had yet to undergo surgery, per Bleacher Report’s James Palmer . No matter how much optimism and determination he may have regarding his return, he will not know anything about his ability to grip a football for weeks. That will be the ultimate test of the rest of the Ravens’ 2026 season.

home.headline: Ravens lose kicker Jake Moody to Falcons, must find replacement before Chargers game
home.blurb: The former third-round draft pick out of Michigan was subsequently returned to Baltimore's practice squad before being claimed by Atlanta. Updated on: November 11, 2026 / 10:50 PM EST / CBS Baltimore The Baltimore Ravens are in need of a kicker after the Atlanta Falcons poached Jake Moody from their practice squad on Tuesday. Moody signed with the Falcons and was added to their 53-man roster, the Falcons announced. Moody was elevated to the Ravens' active roster ahead of their 33-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Nov. 5, making a 53-yard field goal in the game. Moody joined the Ravens' practice squad twice this season as the team looked for competition for struggling kicker Tyler Loop. Loop was placed on injured reserve with a groin injury and will miss at least the next three games. He has converted 13 of 17 field goal attempts this season, including just two of five attempts from 40 to 49 yards. However, Loop has also made kicks from 57 and 64 yards, with the latter securing a win over the Dallas Cowboys in Brazil. Moody rejoined Baltimore's practice squad on Oct. 19 and appeared in one game for the Ravens. Now, the Ravens (4-5), who sit in last place in the AFC North, must find another kicker and add him to their 53-man roster before their next game against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football, Nov. 16.

home.headline: Ravens audition kicker replacements after losing Jake Moody to Falcons
home.blurb: Baltimore is working out a group of free-agent kickers Wednesday, including Riley Patterson and Harrison Mevis, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The auditions come as Tyler Loop is on injured reserve and the Ravens prepare to host the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football. Moody handled Baltimore’s kicking duties during Thursday’s 33-10 loss to Jacksonville, connecting on a 53-yard field goal and his only extra-point attempt. Atlanta subsequently signed him from the Ravens’ practice squad, leaving Baltimore needing another replacement before its next game. Loop opened this season as Baltimore’s kicker before a right groin injury landed him on injured reserve Nov. 3. Moody provided an experienced alternative, but his departure means the Ravens must prepare another specialist while Loop remains unavailable. A new kicker will not solve Baltimore’s broader offensive problems, but converting available scoring opportunities remains essential. Wednesday’s workouts are the next step toward filling a vacancy the Ravens briefly appeared to have addressed with Moody. Ravens’ kicking changes approach a franchise first According to ESPN’s Jamison Hensley, using another kicker would mark the first time in the Ravens’ 31-year history that three kickers have handled the position in one season. Before 2026, Baltimore last had two kickers attempt a field goal in the same season in 2011, when Billy Cundiff and Shayne Graham both did so, Hensley noted. The circumstances create a different evaluation from a normal offseason competition. Baltimore needs someone who can step into its operation quickly and deliver dependable results during the regular season. Riley Patterson and Harrison Mevis get an opportunity Patterson and Mevis bring previous NFL kicking experience to the auditions. Their inclusion gives Baltimore options to assess firsthand rather than choosing solely on past statistics or reputation. The Ravens must determine which candidate offers the best combination of accuracy, range, and consistency. Establishing timing with the snap-and-hold operation will also be important once a replacement is chosen. Monday’s matchup gives Baltimore several days to prepare, but the team has little room for another unsettled position. Baltimore acquired Jacoby Brissett from Arizona to give themselves a new starter after Lamar Jackson's latest injury. But will Brissett be able to play against the Jaguars on Thursday? NFL insider Ian Rapoport gave an update on the quarterback position in Baltimore head of Thursday Night Football. "Now the deal is essentially done, but the actual trade I shouldn't say is it's going to be completed today. It's probably going to be completed after the game for a lot of reasons," Rapoport said on Thursday via Good Morning Football. "… The Ravens obviously lost Lamar Jackson for the foreseeable future and Tyler 'Snoop' Huntley for the season so they needed a starting quarterback. So they bring over Brissett, who has familiarity with Israel Wolfork, the quarterbacks coach, and does know the system pretty well." Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Rapoport echoed reports that Brissett will likely make his debut in Week 10 . One important reason is the trade has yet to be finalized. "He now can come over and be their starting quarterback, but not tonight. If the deal isn't finished he's not on the roster, none of that. So Joe Fagnano, the undrafted free agent, is going to start for the Baltimore Ravens tonight," Rapoport added. "After that, Brissett's going to come in, he's going to learn the system with a couple extra days through the weekend. And then he will likely be the starter next week. In the meantime, Joe Fagnano will remain the starter in Week 9. "So the Ravens get through this game, Fagnano starts, [then] try to keep their season afload with Jacoby Brissett, who has plenty of starting experience, waiting on the other side," Rapoport concluded. Hopefully Baltimore can get a much-needed win before Brissett takes over the starting job. Unfortunately, they square off against an AFC superpower on TNF.
